tasks.name: Task details: render descriptions and notes with CompMD
tasks.description:
Render all task text in the details panel (the description, notes, the review note and a blocked task's questions) with CompMD ([site](https://compmd.hakanserce.com), [repo](https://github.com/comp-markdown/compmd)) instead of `src/lib/markdown.ts`, as the design approved with Hakan says: `docs/compmd-rendering-design.md` (it supersedes this task's first description).

## In short
- CompMD only, no second renderer: while it loads the place is empty; if it can't load, the text shows as written. Readers never see CompMD's diagnostics.
- CompMD ships beside the single-file dashboard: a second Vite build bundles the runtime into `plugin/assets/compmd/<version>/` (`compmd.js` and the processor's `.wasm`), served by `atm serve` at `/assets/` (read-only, `.js` and `.wasm`, no symlinks) and loaded on the first panel open. `npm run check` fails when the committed files are stale.
- The page's CSP adds `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` and the asset folder (never `'self'`).
- The dashboard puts one frontmatter in front of every text (never stored): the task's own data as `md.data.task` (its fields and atm's derived values), nothing else: no files, packs, remote data or other host sources. `safeTree` takes out images that aren't `data:` and links atm wouldn't follow before rendering.
- Rendered in host mode by `@compmd/sandbox`, so T-285's Mermaid pack adds a strict frame without changing this.

## Tests
`docs/compmd-rendering-design.md` §6.

notes.text: Design for review with Hakan before implementing: `docs/compmd-rendering-design.md` (shipping CompMD as served assets, the CSP, the untrusted-text settings, three open points in §7).
Approved: Design approved by Hakan (`docs/compmd-rendering-design.md`). Left: implement it (assets and route, CSP, loader, CompMd component in host mode, md.data.task, tests, security doc).

CompMD renders all task text in the panel (design approved). Check in the browser: a rich description (tables, task lists), notes and questions; the `md.data.task` values; the look in light and dark (screenshots regenerate in the release task). Verified: 978 unit, 364 e2e, 548 atm-cli.

tasks.name: Mermaid diagrams in task text: the @comp-markdown/mermaid pack in the strict sandbox
tasks.description:
Mermaid diagrams in task text, as decided in T-284's design (`docs/compmd-rendering-design.md` §3c, "As built" there): the published pack `@comp-markdown/mermaid`, run by `@compmd/sandbox` in a strict frame (an opaque origin with no network), the text itself rendering in the dashboard's page (host mode).

## As built
- Through `@compmd/vite` only (Hakan's direction): `dashboard/compmd.config.json` pins the pack (`0.1.1`), makes it **ambient** (no import line in the frontmatter) and lists it as the only pack (`imports: "listed"`, strict). The asset build runs `compmd()`, which writes the frame documents and the pack's module into the asset folder and gives `virtual:compmd` (`request`, `sandbox`), re-exported by the served module.
- atm serve serves the folder as the plugin's own server does (CORS `*`, frame documents sandboxed); the page's policy gains `frame-src` for the asset folder.
- Components a text defines itself are never given to the sandbox.
- Diagrams follow light and dark mode; a broken diagram, or a module that doesn't match its hash, shows its code in the frame.
- Measured: one diagram 280–390 ms, five 350–510 ms (opening the panel, CompMD's load included).

## Not here
Math stays TeX until CompMD's host mode typesets it (Hakan is fixing that in CompMD). Building Mermaid into the dashboard at build time is to be reconsidered later (§3c, option D).

## Sample content (for trying the rendering)
Hakan's test content for this task's details panel: it shows how task text renders, and is no part of the work. Math shows as its TeX source until CompMD's fix.

```mermaid {alt="A task goes from to do through in progress and review to done, or back to to do on changes"}
flowchart LR
  todo[To do] --> active[In progress]
  active --> review[In review]
  review -->|approved| done[Done]
  review -->|changes requested| active
  active -->|blocked| blocked[Blocked]
  blocked -->|answered| todo
```

| Diagram | Where it renders | Loaded when |
|---|---|---|
| Flowchart | a strict frame | the text has a `mermaid` block |
| Sequence | a strict frame | the same |
| None | the panel itself | never |

- Shipping
  - the pack's module, `dist/mermaid.js`
    - 7.0 MB minified, 1.6 MB gzipped
  - its licences, `dist/LICENSES.md`
- Running
  - one strict frame per diagram
  - the module's hash checked before it runs

Inline math: the cost grows as $n \cdot t_{parse}$ for $n$ diagrams. Display math:

$$
t_{panel} = t_{load} + \sum_{i=1}^{n} t_{parse,i}
$$

notes.text: Mermaid via `@compmd/vite` (pack pinned 0.1.1, ambient, strict). Check: the diagrams in T-285’s sample content in the browser, light and dark; e2e 371, unit 982, atm-cli 548 pass; timings 1 diagram ~300 ms, 5 ~400 ms. Math waits on the CompMD host-mode fix.

tasks.name: Tell agents what task text can use: CompMD and Mermaid diagrams
tasks.description:
Once the details panel renders all task text with CompMD (T-284) and Mermaid diagrams (T-285), the places that tell agents and users what task text may contain are out of date. Decided in T-284's design review (`docs/compmd-rendering-design.md` §3a): agents get **guidance** on writing CompMD, from CompMD's own guide for language models, `llms.txt`; there is no checker for now.

## The guide, shipped with the plugin
- Copy CompMD's `llms.txt` (in the root of `github.com/comp-markdown/compmd`) into `plugin/docs/compmd-llms.txt`, taken at the commit matching the CompMD version the dashboard ships (T-284's pinned npm version), with one header line naming that version and commit. It is updated with CompMD, by hand in the same change as a CompMD bump.
- Skills point to this local copy; they never tell agents to fetch it, or anything else, from the web.

## Change
- `plugin/skills/create-tasks/SKILL.md`: the rule listing what the dashboard renders ("`#`–`####` headings, paragraphs, …; anything else (tables, HTML) shows as text") becomes a short summary of what renders in atm's panel (T-284's settings): GFM (tables, task lists, footnotes), alerts (`> [!NOTE]`), CompMD's core components (layout, `if`, `each`, `value`) and `mermaid` code blocks as diagrams; math shows as TeX source; inputs show but change nothing; pack imports, data from files or URLs, `host:` data and host-language components don't render (their fallback text shows); raw HTML beyond a short allowlist shows as text. The dashboard adds one frontmatter to every text when it renders it (design §3b; nothing is stored in `tasks.json`): task text never starts with one of its own, and gets the current task's data as `md.data.task` (its fields and atm's derived values: `{{md.data.task.status}}`, `::: each {in=(md.data.task.dependencies) as=d}`), and nothing else. Plain Markdown remains the default; suggest a diagram or a component only where it helps (a flow, a state machine, a comparison). For more, read `plugin/docs/compmd-llms.txt` (its ten rules first).
- `plugin/skills/do-task/SKILL.md` and `plugin/skills/loop-tasks/SKILL.md`, where they describe notes and descriptions as Markdown: the same, in a sentence, with the pointer to the guide.
- `plugin/CLAUDE.md`: one line on what task text renders, with the pointer.
- `docs/help.md` (the dashboard's Help): what renders in task details, with a small table and a small Mermaid example.
- `plugin/CHANGELOG.md` and `plugin/WHATS-NEW.md` entries for 0.28.0, the release that ships T-284 and T-285.

## Security review
Skills and `plugin/CLAUDE.md` change, so the release needs the agent-facing review (`CLAUDE.md`, Security; `docs/security-architecture.md` §3). No API key is used for the agent sandbox: write the review of these skill changes in §3.3 instead of a live run, as for earlier releases. It covers the new text and the shipped `compmd-llms.txt`: read the copy in full before committing it, check it tells agents nothing to run, fetch or install (it is a syntax guide; any such line is left out or the copy is not shipped), and note that skills reference it only as a local file.

notes.text: Skills, `plugin/CLAUDE.md` and Help say what task text renders; `plugin/docs/compmd-llms.txt` is CompMD’s llms.txt at v0.3.0, read in full (§3.3 review, no sandbox run). Check the skill wording; changelog and What’s new are under `[Unreleased]` for the release task to date as 0.28.0.

tasks.name: Design: open referenced documents in a CompMD viewer
tasks.description:

## Questions to settle
- **What opens:** which references count (relative links, `files`, requirement IDs mapped to documents), Markdown only or other text too, and how a reference is resolved (from the project root, from the referring document).
- **Where:** a viewer beside the details panel, a full-page view, or a tab; navigation between linked documents, Back, a deep link in the URL (`#doc=…`).
- **How the server serves them:** today `atm serve` serves only the task files (I11, I12). A read-only route for a project's documents: which files (under the project root only, no symlinks out, maybe only tracked by git, a size cap), content types, and what the security document must say.
- **Untrusted content:** documents are as untrusted as task text: the same CompMD settings as T-284 (no raw HTML, no remote data, no code components), images (local only?), and links out.
- **Fallbacks:** a missing file, a binary file, a project folder that moved.

## Output
`docs/compmd-viewer-design.md` with requirements (numbered, like the other designs), the options weighed and the choice; the follow-up tasks proposed through `/atm:create-tasks` once approved.

tasks.name: Design: built-in code reviews recorded in the project (to replace Crit)
tasks.description:
Write a detailed design, reviewed with Hakan (in Crit), for a **full-fledged code review tool built into atm**, recorded in the project, to replace Crit. Hakan's requirements (2026-11-17) are below; the design works them out and checks them against the use cases.

## Sections the design has
Problem, context, proposal, risks, open issues, alternatives considered; and an **appendix of customer use cases / scenarios**, walked through to show the proposal covers each.

## Hakan's requirements (2026-11-17)

### Storage
- Review records are **stored locally, in the project**. The storage is abstracted like the tasks' store (the JsonGit store of atm-db), but the first implementation is files:
  - a **`reviews/` folder under `.agentic-task-manager/`**;
  - **one folder per review, named `CR-1`, `CR-2`, …**: the numbering is **local to the project**;
  - each review's folder holds the **diffs of each round** and the **comments**;
  - the **comments file** (per round? to decide) is a **concise, human-readable representation of each comment chain**, each starting with the **file and range** it is about;
  - each review has a **header section**: a **summary of the changes**, and the review's **status** (approved, sent back for fixes, …).

### Tasks and reviews
- A task **in review** shows **clickable CR links**.
- When a review is **approved** or **sent back**, that is reflected in the **task's review status**.

### The code reviews section
- atm has a **code reviews section, separate from tasks**, with a **search view** and **process capability** (working through reviews).
- A **diff to review** can be a **commit range**, or **unstaged / uncommitted changes**.
- While reviewing, options to render code and documents as **Crit** does: **source, rendered, split, unified**, **jump to the next / previous change**, **mark files viewed**, and so on.
- A review **opens in its own tab**.
- The **Tauri app's sidebar** has a **tab for CRs**.
- **Several rounds** of one CR: see the **whole diff**, or the **diff between selected rounds**.
- When comments are **submitted, agents can listen and respond**.
- **Markdown renders with CompMD**, as the document viewer does.

### Architecture
Three components in atm, **separable when needed into separate apps** (separate crates and Svelte components) **without too much effort**:
1. **Task manager**: what atm is today.
2. **Document viewer**: what task-referenced documents use today.
3. **Code review tool**: uses (2), and relates to (1).

## Questions the earlier draft of this task raised (still to settle in the design)
- **Writing from the browser:** the dashboard only reads today ([I11](docs/security-architecture.md#:~:text=Nothing%20changes%20state%20over%20HTTP)); comments need writes. In the app, Tauri commands (IPC); in the browser, a write route (loopback, the Host check, a per-session token against CSRF), or read-only there. The threat model and invariants in [`docs/security-architecture.md`](docs/security-architecture.md) change with it.
- **Agents:** atm commands to list, add, reply to and resolve comments, and to **wait for a state change** (a round finished, approved) without polling by hand, keeping the claim alive; how the skills use them. Review comments are task text ([I1](docs/security-architecture.md#:~:text=Task%20text%20is%20data%2C%20not%20commands)): data, never instructions to run.
- **Merging:** review records on branches, merged by atm's merge driver or kept per branch.
- **Replacing Crit:** what Crit does that this must cover (plan reviews, sharing a review, syncing comments to a GitHub PR) and what can wait.

## Output
`docs/code-review-design.md`, reviewed with Hakan in Crit; once approved, the follow-up tasks through `/atm-create-tasks`.

tasks.name: Design a clear layer separation in atm: cli, rest api, client, db, common
tasks.description:
Write a design for splitting atm into clear layers, so each part has one job and dependencies run one way. Design only: no code moves in this task; it ends with the follow-up tasks that carry it out.

## Layers (agreed with Hakan)
- **Dashboard**: talks to the REST API only.
- **REST API** and **CLI**: both thin, on top of **atm-lib**; other tools (an MCP server, scripts) may use atm-lib too.
- **atm-lib**: all business logic; a library others can use.
- **db**: one interface for data access, so the storage can move to another model later (e.g. a cloud DB); today's JSON files in git are its first implementation.
- **vcs**: the code's version control (git), apart from git's role as the task store.
- **common**: the data model and shared rules; the dashboard's TypeScript types are generated from it.

## Output
`docs/layered-architecture.md`, reviewed with the user before it is done; the follow-up tasks are added through `/atm:create-tasks` once approved.

tasks.name: Layers step 8: status changes through atm-lib, with conditional writes
tasks.description:
Step 8 of `docs/layered-architecture.md` §9: the first writes on the new path (§3.3).

## Change
- Conditional writes (`update_task(…, expect=version)`, `Conflict` on a stale version) and `apply(writes)` (all or nothing) in both stores; the JSON-in-git store's `apply` is today's lock, read, write.
- `start`, `review`, `done`, `reject`, `approve`, `request-changes`, `block`, `unblock`, `reopen`, `skip`, `fail`, `release` and `note` as atm-lib functions (§5.1); the claim created or dropped in the same `apply`; atm-lib retries on `Conflict`.
- `tasks.py`'s direct locking and writing goes; the ratchet shrinks.

## Tests
- `tests/lib/` tests for each function, including a race (two starts of one task: one wins, the other gets `claimed`); contract tests for conditional writes and `apply` on both stores.
- `npm run test:scripts` (the concurrency tests included) and `npm run test:e2e` pass.

notes.text: Status changes vs §3.3: (A) rework them into entity writes (task update + claim create/drop) with versions, `apply`, retry on `Conflict` — the design’s contract now, a bigger change; or (B) a transitional store operation running today’s locked read-modify-write (like `document()`), conditional writes in a later step — smaller, but the generic transaction the design rejected, for a while. Which? → B: a store `change(fn)` running the locked read-modify-write on a `Working` copy, which records what fn changed (before/after per task and claim) so a store can later turn it into conditional writes (`apply`); `work.defer(error)` for raise-after-write. Update §3.3 to say so.

Check: option B. `store.change(fn)` with a `Working` copy (`db/working.py`: tasks, claims, here, size, defer; `changes()` worked out only when asked, from the unwritten files), JSON store under its lock, memory store on copies; the 13 status commands and `note` in `lib/status.py`, printing in `cli/status.py`; `tasks.py` gone from the ratchet. §3.3 updated. Benchmark: 10k-task write 0.89 s, same as before (0.90 s). 540 atm-cli, 64 `tests/lib`.

tasks.name: Tolerant reads: the dashboard keeps showing a malformed task file, with what atm finds wrong
tasks.description:
Since T-365 the dashboard loads tasks through atm-lib (`GET /api/v1/projects/<id>/tasks`), which refuses a task file every `atm` command refuses (`load_tasks` in `model.py`: an entry without a string `id`, an ID with characters atm doesn't allow, `dependencies` that aren't a list of IDs, an unusable vocabulary). The dashboard used to show such a file anyway. Keep that, as agreed with Hakan (option 1).

## Change
- A tolerant read mode in the store (`JsonGitStore`, and the in-memory store): writes stay strict, reads keep what they can. An entry that isn't a task (no string `id`) is left out; a task with a bad ID or bad `dependencies` is kept; an unusable vocabulary falls back to the defaults (as `dashboard/src/lib/vocab.ts` already does).
- Each problem is reported: per task as `derived.problems` (a list of messages, the wording of `atm check`), and for the file as a top-level `problems` list in the v1 response (`api.schema.json`). The rules skip what they can't judge: a task with broken `dependencies` isn't `ready` and waits for nothing it can name.
- The REST API's v1 tasks route reads tolerantly; every `atm` command stays strict.
- The dashboard shows a notice when `problems` isn't empty (e.g. "atm check finds 3 problems in tasks.json"), and a task's problems in its detail panel.

## Tests
- `tests/lib/`: the tolerant read on both stores (contract tests), `task_views` with each kind of problem.
- `tests/scripts/serve.test.mjs`: the v1 route serves a malformed file with `problems`, where `atm list` still refuses it.
- The e2e fixture's fallback (`asTaskViews` in `tests/e2e/helpers.ts`, empty derived values when atm refuses a file) goes: it takes atm's tolerant views. Unit and e2e tests for the notice.
- Update `docs/multi-project-api.md` §2.5 and `docs/layered-architecture.md` §3.

notes.text: Check: `load_tasks_tolerant` + `JsonGitStore(tolerant=True)`/`problems()`; the v1 route reads tolerantly (commands stay strict): non-task entries left out, bad IDs kept, broken deps shown with the readable IDs (every task fits the schema; a string there used to break the page), unusable vocab lists → defaults; `derived.problems` (not ready) + response `problems`. Footer notice, detail list. `atm list --derived --tolerant`. 955 unit, 359 e2e, 541 atm-cli.

tasks.name: Layers gap 11.4: pass the archive lookup to the rules; the global hook goes (fixes a server race)
tasks.description:
`docs/layered-architecture.md` §11.4. Before the branch is merged.

## Problem
`common/model.py`'s `use_archive`/`archived_task` is a module-global lookup the JSON-in-git store's loaders set. `atm serve` is threaded and serves many projects in one process, so a request for one project can be judged against another project's archive (a dependency only in its own archive counts as missing; a ready task shows as waiting). On the in-memory store the hook is never set.

## Change
- The rules take the lookup as a parameter: `unfinished_dependencies(data, task, archived)`, `find_task(data, id, archived=...)`, `change_status`, the checks in `lib/edit.py` and `lib/status.py`, `cli/render.py`.
- atm-lib passes `store.get_archived_task`, or `archived_in(work)` inside a change.
- Each store keeps its own lazy archive cache (`JsonGitStore.get_archived_task` reads its own archive).
- `use_archive`, `_archive` and the global `archived_task` are deleted.
- Update §11.4 (settled) and §8's paragraph on the hook.

## Tests
- `tests/lib/`: a dependency only in the archive counts as done, on both stores (contract test).
- Two JSON-in-git projects used one after the other in one process never see each other's archives.
- `npm run test:scripts`; the serve tests.

notes.text: The global archive lookup is gone: the rules take the project’s lookup (`store.get_archived_task`, or `archived_in(work)` in a change), required where readiness depends on it; each store caches its own archive. Fixes the `atm serve` race (one project judged by another’s archive). New contract tests: archive-only dependency is done on both stores; two projects in one process. 540 + 126 pass.

tasks.name: Layers gap 11.1: two launchers, atm and an internal atm-serve, replace the app layer
tasks.description:
`docs/layered-architecture.md` §11.1.

## Change
- `plugin/scripts/atm` runs the CLI; a new internal launcher `plugin/scripts/atm-serve` runs the REST API's server (one dispatch at the bottom of the one built `atm.py`, e.g. a `--server` entry).
- The CLI manages the server as a process: `atm serve start|stop|status` spawn `atm-serve`, signal it and read its record; the restart after a plugin update spawns it too.
- The cheap refresh check every command runs stays in-process: the server record's format and the dashboard's version tags (`api/dashboard.py`) move into common.
- `app/` and `cli/main.py`'s `Serving` go; the layer rule drops `app`. The CLI never imports `api`.
- `atm serve` and every skill, hook and permission stay exactly as they are (no new command for users or agents).
- Update §1's diagram and table, §8's layout, §11.1 (settled), `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/v4/atm-cli.md`.

## Tests
- The serve tests pass unchanged; a build test that the CLI may not import the API stays.
- `npm run test:scripts`.

notes.text: The `app` layer is gone: the CLI (`plugin/scripts/atm`) and the server (`plugin/scripts/atm-serve`, `atm.py --server`) are two processes; `atm serve` lives in `cli/serve.py`, the server process in `api/server.py` (`serve_main`); shared tags and record names in `common/dashboard.py`; the build writes the one entry and checks layers before order. 541 tests pass; users see no change.

tasks.name: Layers gap 11.2: split boot into what every store has and what only the JSON-in-git store has

## Tests

notes.text: boot is split: `boot/open.py` (any store: `open_project`, `open_registry`, `project_opener` for atm serve) and `boot/jsongit.py` (this store only: paths, migrate, merge driver, setup, lock test, registering by folder). `cli/store.py` imports only `boot/jsongit.py`; the REST API only `boot/open.py`. 541 + 126 pass.

tasks.name: Layers gap 11.3: change(fn) as the write path by design; per-entity reads; the store private to atm-lib and boot
tasks.description:
`docs/layered-architecture.md` §11.3.

## Change
- §3.2 and §3.3 say what is built: `store.change(fn)` with the `Working` copy and its change list is the write path (no per-entity writes, no `apply`); list the interface as it is.
- Add per-entity reads to the Store interface and both stores: `list_sprints`, `list_releases`, `list_components`, `get_settings` (meta without the lists).
- Move atm-lib's reads off `store.document()` area by area (sprints, releases, components, settings, code, query); `document()` remains only as `work.document` inside a change, then goes from the interface.
- `Project`'s store becomes private (`project._store`); the REST API and the CLI get what they read from atm-lib functions (the v1 route's meta, the server's stamps and working copies, `atm logo`'s working copy).
- A build check refuses `.store.` / `._store` outside `lib/` and `boot/`.
- Update §3.2, §3.3, §11.3 (settled).

## Tests
- Contract tests for each new read on both stores; a build test for the `.store` check; `npm run test:scripts`.

notes.text: change(fn) is the write path by design (§3.2/3.3). New per-entity reads (settings, sprints, releases, components) on both stores; the CLI and REST API no longer touch `project.store` (`task_snapshot`, `project_stamp`, `working_copies`), and the build refuses `.store` there. Left, by the review’s choice: ~12 reads still take `document()` because the rules take the whole file (§11.3). 542 pass.

tasks.name: Layers gap 11.10 B: nullable types in the generator; ProjectSummary and StatusReport in the schema
tasks.description:
`docs/layered-architecture.md` §11.10 B.

## Change

- `api.schema.json` gets `ProjectSummary` (what `api/projects` gives per project: totals, sprints, board, stats, git, needs you, …) and `StatusReport` (`atm status --json`).
- The dashboard's hand-written `ProjectSummary` (`dashboard/src/lib/load.ts`) is replaced by the generated type.
- Update §4.1, §4.2, §11.10 B (settled).

## Tests

- A test validates a real `atm summary` and `atm status --json` and the e2e fixture's summary against the schema (as the fixtures are validated today).
- `npm run check`, the unit tests, `npm run test:scripts`.

notes.text: The generator takes nullable types (`[T, "null"]`, `anyOf` with null) and maps; `api.schema.json` has `ProjectSummary` and `StatusReport`; the Dashboard re-exports the generated types. `tests/lib/test_schema.py` checks real summaries and status reports (busy, empty, every fixture). Check: the older-server fallbacks are left (§11.10 B).

tasks.name: Layers gap 11.7: atm-lib's public functions as §5.1 lists them
tasks.description:
`docs/layered-architecture.md` §11.7.

tasks.name: Add the tenets to the README
tasks.description:
Add a short **Tenets** section to `README.md`: the principles atm is built on, one line each with a sentence on what it means for a user.

## The tenets
- **The data lives with the project**, versioned with the project's own version control (`.agentic-task-manager/` in the repository, committed with the code).
- **One skill install**: installing the plugin is all it takes; nothing else to set up (no service, no account, no database).
- **Actions through agents**: every change to the tasks is made by an agent running a skill (or `atm`), not by hand in the files.
- **Visibility through the dashboard**: the dashboard shows everything and is read-only.

## Notes
Place it near the top, after the introduction. Keep the README's tone; don't restate details covered further down, link to them instead.

notes.text: README has a Tenets section after the intro (data with the project, one skill install, actions through agents, read-only dashboard), each linking to its details. Three passages that said to edit tasks.json or the dashboard by hand now say to use an agent or `atm`.

tasks.name: atm serve loses track of a running server: stop and status miss it, and it keeps running
tasks.description:
Found 2026-11-03: two dashboard servers kept running on ports 8765 and 8766, serving the real `~/.agentic-task-manager`. They were started on Nov 2, 8 minutes apart, from the repository checkout's `atm.py` (`_serve-child`, before T-379). `atm serve stop` and `atm serve status` said no server was running, because the server record (`SERVER_RECORD` in the user's atm folder) named another server, which had been stopped. The two had to be stopped by hand.

## Likely causes (check each with a test first)
- `stop_server` in `atm-cli/atm/cli/serve.py` sends SIGTERM, waits until a deadline, then removes the record **whether or not the process exited**. A server that outlives the wait (as during a `--refresh` restart) is left running with no record, and the new server takes the next free port.
- Two `ensure_server` calls at once (two sessions' SessionStart hooks, or the hook and `/atm:serve`) both find no live record, and each starts a server; the second overwrites the record.
- Servers from another plugin root (a checkout versus the installed plugin) share one record.

## Change
- `stop_server`: if the process is still alive after the wait, escalate (SIGKILL) or keep the record and report it, never forget a live server.
- Starting: hold a lock in the atm folder across "is one running?" → start → write the record, so only one server is started.
- `atm serve status` and `stop`: also find an atm server that answers `whoami` on the usual ports (8765 upward) for this atm folder but isn't the recorded one, report it, and let `stop` stop it (it is ours: `whoami` says `atm: true` and gives its pid).

## Tests
`tests/scripts/serve.test.mjs`: a server that ignores the first SIGTERM is still stopped (or reported) by `stop`; two `atm serve start` at once leave one server; `stop` finds and stops a server whose record was overwritten.

notes.text: Fixed all three causes, each with a test: `stop` escalates to SIGKILL and drops the record only once the server is gone; starting holds `ATM_HOME/server.lock`; `status`/`stop` find this folder’s unrecorded servers on 20 ports from `--port` via `home` in whoami (a path hash). atm-cli 551 pass.

tasks.name: Text-fragment links: references open the document at the text, and agents write them that way
tasks.description:
References to a requirement, a use case or any place in a document are **links with a text fragment** (decided with Hakan while planning; no ID index): `[SR-2.1](docs/sprints-and-releases-design.md#:~:text=SR%2D2.1)`. The viewer opens the document at the first match and highlights it; GitHub and browsers understand the same links.

## Text fragments
The [text fragment](https://web.dev/articles/text-fragments#text_fragments) syntax: `#:~:text=[prefix-,]textStart[,textEnd][,-suffix]`, each part percent-encoded. `-`, `,` and `&` are part of the syntax, so in the text they are `%2D`, `%2C` and `%26` (an ID `SR-2.1` is `SR%2D2.1`). `textStart,textEnd` matches a range; `prefix-,` and `,-suffix` only narrow which match is meant. Several `text=` directives may follow, joined by `&`.

## Change
- `dashboard/src/lib/documents.ts`: parse a link's `#:~:text=…` (alone, or after a `#heading` fragment, which then gives way to it): decode the parts, find the first match in the rendered document's text (case-insensitive, across inline elements, whitespace collapsed; `textEnd` the end of the range; prefix and suffix checked around it), scroll to it and mark it (a highlight in the theme's colours, gone at the next click). No match: open at the top, with a short note that the text wasn't found. Unit tests for the parser and the matcher.
- The details panel: each `requirements` and `use_cases` entry renders inline with CompMD, so an entry written as a link (`[SR-2.1](docs/x.md#:~:text=SR%2D2.1)`) opens the viewer; a bare ID stays text, as now.
- **Skills** (`plugin/skills/create-tasks/SKILL.md`, and the lines on task text in `do-task`, `loop-tasks` and `plugin/CLAUDE.md`): from now on, a reference to a requirement, a use case or a place in a document is a relative link from the project root with a text fragment, and `requirements` / `use_cases` entries are such links. Say what a text fragment is, how its parts work, and the encoding of `-`, `,` and `&`, with two examples (an ID; a phrase with a prefix). A skill change: add the written review to `docs/security-architecture.md` §3.3 (no API key for the agent sandbox).
- `docs/help.md`: references open the document at the text.

## Try it
Each opens the document viewer at the text, marked until the next click:

| What | Link |
|---|---|
| An ID, its `-` encoded | [SR-2.1](docs/sprints-and-releases-design.md#:~:text=SR%2D2.1) |
| Another ID, in a long table | [SR-7.6](docs/sprints-and-releases-design.md#:~:text=SR%2D7.6) |
| A phrase after a heading (a prefix) | [A link in task text](docs/compmd-viewer-design.md#:~:text=Resolving%20a%20reference-,A%20link%20in) |
| The second of two matches (a suffix) | [Placement, as decided](docs/compmd-viewer-design.md#:~:text=Placement%3A,-A%2C%20movable) |
| A range, from one text to another | [the review's decisions](docs/compmd-viewer-design.md#:~:text=Decided%20in%20the%20first%20round,Not%20only%20Markdown) |
| An invariant, by its words | [I11](docs/security-architecture.md#:~:text=Nothing%20changes%20state%20over%20HTTP) |
| Text the document doesn't have | [nowhere](docs/compmd-viewer-design.md#:~:text=no%20such%20sentence) (opens at the top, saying so) |

A `requirements` entry written as a link shows in the details panel as a link too: this task's **Requirements** have two (V1d, V2, each opening the viewer at its text) and a bare ID (V2a, which stays text). On its card, all three show as text.

## Tests
Unit tests (parsing, encoding, matching with prefix, suffix and ranges); a component test for requirement links in the details panel; e2e: a text-fragment link in a description and in `requirements` opens the viewer at the match and marks it; one that matches nothing opens at the top with the note.

notes.text: Text-fragment links open the document at the text, marked (CSS Custom Highlight API, CompMD’s page untouched); `requirements`/`use_cases` entries may be links. Check the skills’ wording on references (create-tasks, do-task, loop-tasks, plugin/CLAUDE.md) and the §3.3 written review. e2e 401, unit 1010; single file 554 kB.

tasks.name: Document viewer: atm-lib read_file and the documents and files routes
tasks.description:
The server side of the document viewer, as `docs/compmd-viewer-design.md` §4 and §7 say.

## Change
- atm-lib `read_file(project, path)`: what a file is (§4a: `markdown`, `code` with its language from an extension map, `image`, `binary`, `text`), its `text` as it is, the CompMD `document` to render (code and text in a fence longer than any backtick run in them), `line_offset` (1 for a fence, 0 for Markdown), `lines`, `bytes`, `modified_at`.
- For the viewer's *Open on GitHub* (T-393): `tracked` (git tracks the file) and `commit` (the HEAD commit's SHA), both through the vcs layer; `null` outside a git repository.
- The checks of §4b: a relative, normalized path (no `..`, `.`, empty or hidden segment, no NUL or backslash, at most 512 characters); no symlink anywhere from the project root; not a file git ignores; not a key file (`*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.p12`, `*.pfx`, `id_rsa*`, `id_ed25519*`, `*.keystore`); a regular file of at most 1 MB (5 MB for images); a registered project. A project that isn't a git repository: no ignore check (the other checks hold).
- REST: `GET api/v1/projects/<id>/documents?path=…` (JSON) and `GET api/v1/projects/<id>/files?path=…` (an image's bytes only, with its `Content-Type`, `nosniff`, CORP same-origin and `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox`), both with an ETag of size and mtime (304 when unchanged).
- `docs/security-architecture.md`: I11 (the routes and their checks), I12 (what of a project the server reads now), and a §3.3 entry.

## Not here
Rendering: the server only wraps a file into a CompMD document (a fence with the file's language for code); CompMD
renders it, highlighting included.

## Tests
`tests/lib/` for the kinds, the wrapping, `line_offset`, `tracked` and `commit`; `serve.test.mjs` for every check (a hidden file, an ignored one, a key file, a symlinked folder, `..`, too big), the ETag and the image headers.

notes.text: Routes `documents?path=` and `files?path=` through `lib/documents.py` (path rules, kinds, wrapping) and the vcs (reading, `ignored`, `tracked`, `head`). Check: `serve.test.mjs` "a project’s files for the document viewer"; note the ignore check fails closed (it first failed open: `check-ignore` refuses `--literal-pathspecs`). atm-cli 552 pass.

tasks.name: Document viewer: the window, the #doc= hash and Back
tasks.description:
The viewer window of `docs/compmd-viewer-design.md` §2 and §6. **Reviewed live with Hakan on the dev server** before the tasks that build on it (review mode `blocker`).

## Change
- `dashboard/src/lib/documents.ts`: resolving a reference (§3: from the project root for task text, from the document's folder inside a document, never leaving the project), the URL hash (`#doc=<path>`, with `:L<n>`), fetching the documents route through `src/lib/api/http.ts` with its ETag on the dashboard's poll.
- `dashboard/src/components/DocumentViewer.svelte`: stacked over the details panel, slightly offset; movable by its title bar (pointer, and arrow keys on the focused title bar), kept inside the window; resizable from a visible grip on its bottom-right corner (Shift and the arrow keys too), with a minimum size; its position and size kept in the local preferences; a thin themed scrollbar; full-window without move or resize on a narrow window. Back (the button, Escape, the browser's Back) returns to the previous document or the task. The fallbacks of V6.
- **The title bar:** the document's first heading (else its file name), its path under it, and two actions (decided with Hakan):
  - **Copy path**: copies the path from the project root, with `#L<n>` (or `#L<n>-L<m>`) when a line or range is selected, for pasting to an agent; says "Copied" for a moment.
  - **Open on GitHub**: the file in the repository's web view (`meta.repository`, the same address rules as commit links), at the HEAD commit the documents route gives (`commit`), with the selected line; in a new tab, without access to the page. Shown only when the project has a repository address and git tracks the file (`tracked`).
- `CompMd.svelte` takes a document's request parts (its own frontmatter, no `host:` data, only this file in `files`).

## Tests
Unit tests for `documents.ts` (resolving, the hash, the GitHub address); e2e: open, move, resize, Back, Reload keeps it, Copy path (with a line), Open on GitHub (shown or not), a missing file, a refused file.

notes.text: Live review on the dev server: open `#doc=docs/compmd-viewer-design.md` with the task panel open; move by the title bar, resize from the corner, Reload, Back, Escape, Copy path (`:L3`), Open on GitHub, a narrow window. e2e 386, unit 1001 pass.

tasks.name: Document viewer: line numbers, refreshing in place, images
tasks.description:
Rendering in the viewer, `docs/compmd-viewer-design.md` §4a and §5.

## Change
- **Line numbers** in a gutter on the left of a `code` or `text` file: a number per line of `text` (its lines never wrap on screen: the block scrolls sideways). `#L<n>` scrolls to the line; `#L<n>-L<m>` marks the range. Markdown documents are T-400: their blocks' source lines come from CompMD's renderer, through an API it is adding.
- **Links to the dashboard itself** (its own address with a `#…`, e.g. a document's URL) open in place instead of in a new tab (Hakan, while trying this task's links).
- **Refreshing in place:** a changed file re-renders where the reader is, never back at the top. A 304 changes nothing.
- **Images:** a relative Markdown image becomes the files route's URL for the path resolved from the document's folder; `data:` stays; any other image shows its alt text.

## Not here
Rendering content: CompMD renders the whole document, code blocks and their highlighting included (it takes care of highlighting itself); atm only wraps a file into a CompMD document (the server, T-392). The gutter, the line-range mark and the scroll position are the viewer's own UI around CompMD's output; add no renderer or highlighter.

## Try it
On the dev server (`npm run dev` in `dashboard/`), these open in a new tab; once T-395 is done, the relative links below open the viewer in place.

| What | Dev server | In the dashboard (T-395) |
|---|---|---|
| A design, lines 14–20 marked | [open](http://localhost:5174/#project=cb66fd8c&view=list&doc=docs/compmd-viewer-design.md:L14-L20) | [docs/compmd-viewer-design.md#L14-L20](docs/compmd-viewer-design.md#L14-L20) |
| Code, line 40 | [open](http://localhost:5174/#project=cb66fd8c&view=list&doc=atm-cli/atm/lib/documents.py:L40) | [atm-cli/atm/lib/documents.py#L40](atm-cli/atm/lib/documents.py#L40) |
| Code, a range | [open](http://localhost:5174/#project=cb66fd8c&view=list&doc=dashboard/src/lib/documents.ts:L44-L60) | [dashboard/src/lib/documents.ts#L44-L60](dashboard/src/lib/documents.ts#L44-L60) |
| An image | [open](http://localhost:5174/#project=cb66fd8c&view=list&doc=branding/atm-logo.png) | [branding/atm-logo.png](branding/atm-logo.png) |
| A document in another folder | [open](http://localhost:5174/#project=cb66fd8c&view=list&doc=branding/README.md) | [branding/README.md](branding/README.md) |

## Tests
e2e: the gutter and the code are the same height; `#L40` opens at line 40 and marks it; a changed file re-renders at the same place; a local image loads from this server and a remote one doesn't; a link to the dashboard opens in place.

Code and text files: gutter, `:L40-L45` scrolls and marks; refreshing keeps the place; relative images load from the files route; links to the dashboard open in place. Check with the links in this task’s description. Markdown lines are T-400 (blocked on CompMD’s renderer API). e2e 394, unit 1003; single file 549 kB (guardrail 550 KiB).

tasks.name: atm commit: a folder's changes at once, with --dir
tasks.description:
`atm commit` takes files only one `--file` at a time and refuses folders, so that it never commits another agent's work in the same tree. A generated folder makes that a chore: T-398 had to name 230 files of `plugin/assets/compmd/` (the old version's removed, the new one's added) one by one.

## Change
- `atm commit <id> --dir <folder>` (repeatable, beside `--file`): every change git sees under the folder, as `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` lists it (modified, added, deleted, renamed, new files git doesn't ignore), committed with the other files and `tasks.json`. The output names each file, as now.
- Still refused, with a message: `.` and the repository's root (or anything above it), `.agentic-task-manager/`, a path outside the repository, and a folder with no changes. A changed file under the folder that another task **in progress and claimed by another agent** lists in its `files` makes the whole commit refuse, naming the file and the task: that is the case the rule against folders is there for.
- [`atm-cli/atm/cli/`](atm-cli/atm/cli/) (the option) and atm-lib's `commit_task` (the expansion, through the vcs layer; `tests/lib/public-surface.json` and the changelog if its signature changes).
- The skills' commit steps (`/atm:do-task` Step 7, `/atm:loop-tasks` step 5, [`plugin/CLAUDE.md`](plugin/CLAUDE.md)'s *Commit* line): `--dir` for a generated folder the task rebuilt, never for a folder others work in. A skill change and a CLI option that reads a path: a written review in [`docs/security-architecture.md`](docs/security-architecture.md) §3.3, and the invariant on `atm commit` updated.

## Tests
Scenarios or `*.test.mjs` in `tests/scripts/` (a git repository): a folder with a modified, a new and a deleted file commits all three and nothing outside it; `.`, the root, `.agentic-task-manager/` and an empty folder are refused; another agent's claimed task listing a changed file under the folder refuses the commit and commits nothing.

notes.text: Check: `atm commit --dir FOLDER` commits a folder’s changes (modified, new, deleted, renamed); refuses the root, outside, the task folder, a file, nothing changed, and another agent’s claimed files. Skills and CLAUDE.md say: generated folders only. §3.3 review; public surface + `folder_changes`. atm-cli 559.

tasks.name: Upgrade CompMD to 0.5.0, and number every line of a Markdown document in the viewer's gutter
tasks.description:
T-400 numbers a Markdown document's blocks, each with its first source line (1, 4, 6, 9…), because CompMD 0.4.0 maps a source offset to the **elements** its node drew (`view.rectsAt`), not to a place in the text: a paragraph written over two lines is one box, so its second line has no place of its own. Hakan: CompMD 0.5.0 adds text-precise positions. When it is out, the gutter numbers every source line, as an editor does.

## Change
- Upgrade `@compmd/processor`, `@compmd/render`, `@compmd/sandbox` and `@compmd/vite` to 0.5.0, as T-398 did for 0.4.0: its *Change* list (the runtime folder, `plugin/docs/compmd-llms.txt` read in full, the §3.3 line, the release notes' changes for hosts) applies again. Restart a running `npm run dev` with `--force` after the install.
- The gutter in [`DocumentViewer.svelte`](dashboard/src/components/DocumentViewer.svelte) for a Markdown document: a number for each source line that draws something, at its exact place through CompMD 0.5.0's text-precise lookup (read its README for the call: a line's start offset to its box in the rendered text); a line that starts with markup (`**bold…`) at the element it starts. Blank lines draw nothing: their numbers go in the gaps between blocks, spread over the gap, so the column reads 1, 2, 3… with no line skipped.
- `:L<n>-L<m>` marks exactly those lines, not their whole blocks; Copy path and Open on GitHub as now.
- Replaces T-400's per-block numbers (`blockSources`/`placeBlocks` in [`lib/compmd.ts`](dashboard/src/lib/compmd.ts)): keep what still serves, remove the rest.
- Never match rendered text to source text to find a line: what drew a line is CompMD's to say (T-400's rule).

## Tests
Unit tests for the line placement; e2e: a paragraph written over two lines gets two numbers, each beside its words; a frontmatter's lines counted; blank lines numbered in the gaps; `:L7` marks the paragraph's second line only; the existing code-file gutter tests unchanged. Reviewed with Hakan in the browser.

tasks.name: Files inside a git submodule open in the document viewer
tasks.description:
A file inside a git submodule never opens in the viewer: it says the file can't be shown, as for a file git ignores (Hakan).

## Cause
The vcs layer's [`ignored`](atm-cli/atm/vcs/git.py#:~:text=def%20ignored) runs `git check-ignore` in the project's repository. For a path inside a submodule, git refuses ("is in submodule", exit 128), and the check fails closed: any answer but "not ignored" counts as ignored. [`tracked`](atm-cli/atm/vcs/git.py#:~:text=def%20tracked) has the same problem (`ls-files` in the superproject doesn't list the submodule's files), so *Open on GitHub* would be wrong for them too.

## Change
- `ignored` and `tracked` in [`atm-cli/atm/vcs/git.py`](atm-cli/atm/vcs/git.py): for a path inside a submodule (the nearest submodule from `git submodule status`, or `git ls-files --stage` mode `160000`, cached per call), ask the submodule's own git with the path relative to it. Its ignore rules, and the superproject's for the submodule's folder, decide; any other git error still refuses (fail closed, as now). Nested submodules: the innermost.
- `head`/`tracked` for *Open on GitHub*: a file in a submodule links to the submodule's own repository at its commit, when its remote is a web address atm knows (`repo.ts`'s hosts); otherwise the button doesn't show. Through the documents route's `tracked`/`commit` fields, plus what the link needs (the submodule's web address and path).
- The other checks stay as they are for submodule files: no hidden parts, no key files, no symlink on the way, the size limits.
- [`docs/security-architecture.md`](docs/security-architecture.md): I11 and I12 say what the routes do inside a submodule (its own ignore rules; failing closed).

## Tests
`serve.test.mjs` with a real submodule (a second repository added with `git submodule add` from a local path): a file in it opens; one its `.gitignore` ignores doesn't; a key file in it doesn't; the documents route gives the submodule's commit. A unit test in `tests/lib/` for the path-to-submodule lookup.

notes.text: Check: files in a submodule open (its own ignore rules, failing closed); Open on GitHub goes to the submodule’s repo at its commit. `serve.test.mjs` “files in a git submodule…” with a real submodule; I11/I12 updated. e2e 409, atm-cli 556.

tasks.name: Dashboard: SvelteKit with the static adapter
tasks.description:
Move the dashboard from plain Svelte + Vite to SvelteKit, as the [Svelte guide](docs/guides/svelte.md#basics) asks.

## Change
- SvelteKit 3 with the static adapter and an SPA fallback; its options in the `sveltekit({ … })` call in `vite.config.ts`; `svelte.config.js` removed; `tsconfig.json` extends `$app/tsconfig`.
- The build still writes **one self-contained HTML file** to `plugin/templates/tasks-dashboard.html` (with the `atm-dashboard-version` meta tag) and the CompMD runtime to `plugin/assets/compmd/<version>/`, and `atm serve` serves it under the same Content-Security-Policy (invariants I13 and I16 in [security-architecture.md](docs/security-architecture.md)). The dev server (`build/dev-api.ts`, `build/security-headers.ts`) keeps working.
- No change in behaviour: the hash routes stay until the next task.

If SvelteKit's static output can't be made into the single file (or only at a cost in size or CSP), stop and block the task on the user with the options found, rather than changing the single-file or CSP rules.

## Tests
`check`, the unit tests, `tests/scripts/dev-api.test.mjs` and the functional e2e suite pass; `size` is no larger than before by more than a few KB.

notes.text: Prototype (undone): SvelteKit 3.1.1 + `adapter-static` (SPA fallback) + `output.bundleStrategy: inline` gives one HTML file, with one inline script and no `eval`, which `atm serve`’s per-script hashes allow. Size: 635 KB against 575 KB (+60 KB, +10%), 195 against 172 KB gzipped. `router.type: hash` can’t be used: SvelteKit takes over `location.hash`, where the dashboard keeps its state. Its own `history.pushState`/`replaceState` calls (`state.svelte.ts`) would move to `$app/navigation`.

SvelteKit fits the single file and the security policy, but adds about 60 KB (+10%; +23 KB gzipped) for its runtime, over the few KB this task allows. Accept that and migrate? Or keep plain Svelte + Vite and drop SvelteKit from the guide (T-429 then gives real routes with a small router of our own)? Or defer it until the atm app needs SvelteKit? → Accept the +60 KB (+10%) for SvelteKit and migrate.

SvelteKit 3.1.1 + adapter-static, inline bundle: still one file (636 KB, +60 KB as agreed; guardrail 650 KiB); finish-page.ts stamps it; catch-all route; dev CSP per page. Review: vite.config.ts, security-headers.ts.

tasks.description:

## Change
- SvelteKit routes replace `src/lib/routes.ts` and `src/lib/hash.ts`; back, forward and deep links keep working.
- `atm serve` answers the new paths with the page (SPA fallback), without serving anything else under them; the routes go into [multi-project-api.md](docs/multi-project-api.md).
- Old `#…` links (bookmarks, links in task text) redirect to the new addresses.
- The new paths are entry points: update [security-architecture.md](docs/security-architecture.md) in the same change.

## Tests
Unit tests for the route mapping and the redirect of old links; `serve.test.mjs` for the fallback; the e2e specs that navigate (tabs, detail, documents, projects) use the new addresses.

notes.text: Address scheme (each path becomes an atm serve entry point): `/` the overview, `/board` `/progress` `/agents` its tabs; `/projects/<id>` a project, `/projects/<id>/<tab>` its tabs; details and documents as `?task=T-1` and `?doc=docs/x.md#L40` over any view; sprint and dialogs as query parameters. Old `#…` links redirect. OK? → The proposed scheme, as is: `/` overview (`/board`, `/progress`, `/agents`), `/projects/<id>[/<tab>]`, `?task=` and `?doc=` in the query; old `#…` links redirect.; Or task and document as path segments instead (`/projects/<id>/tasks/T-1`, `/projects/<id>/docs/<path>`)? → (no answer)

tasks.name: Dashboard: pin pnpm and Node with devEngines, once CompMD reads pnpm 12's lockfile
tasks.description:
T-427 moved the dashboard to pnpm without the `devEngines` pins the [Svelte guide](docs/guides/svelte.md#toolchain) asks for, because of a CompMD bug: with `devEngines`, pnpm 12 writes `pnpm-lock.yaml` as two YAML documents (the pinned pnpm and Node first, then the packages), and `@compmd/vite` 0.5.0 reads only the first document that has `packages` (`dist/packs.js`, `integrities`). The mermaid pack's `integrity` then becomes `null` in `plugin/assets/compmd/<version>/compmd.js`, and its pin is lost.

**Wait for** a `@compmd/vite` release that reads every document of the lockfile. Until then this task stays in the backlog.

## Change
- Bump `@compmd/vite` (and the other `@compmd/*` packages it goes with) to that release.
- Add `devEngines` to `dashboard/package.json`: `packageManager` pnpm 12.14.0 (or the version in use then) and `runtime` node 24, both with `"onFail": "download"`, as in the guide; `pnpm install` records them in the lockfile.
- Update the guide's example version if it changed, and AGENTS.md if it says the pins are missing.

## Tests
`pnpm run build`, then `compmd.js` holds the mermaid pack's `integrity` (a `sha512-…`, not `null`); `pnpm run check` passes (it fails on a stale CompMD build); unit and functional e2e tests; CI green.

notes.text: Waits for a `@compmd/vite` release that reads every document of `pnpm-lock.yaml` (the CompMD task the user is creating in that project). Unblock it once that release is out.
CompMD 0.6.0 is out (T-503 uses it) and reads every document of pnpm 12’s lockfile (Hakan): go ahead.

`devEngines` pins pnpm 12.14.0 and Node 24 (`onFail: download`), recorded in `pnpm-lock.yaml` (now two documents); CompMD 0.7.1 still pins the packs by hash (no null integrity). AGENTS.md updated. CI green still to see on the next push

Fix (855d3ed): the dev page was blank on Node 24.22 (the pinned Node): the page-policy hold on `writeHead` swallowed the head Node sends from `end`, so every module came without one; and a reload got a 304 whose policy lacked the inline scripts’ hashes. Pages are now never answered 304, a 304 carries no policy; `dev-api.test.mjs` fetches modules and reloads

tasks.name: Remove atm run; atm claim hold keeps a claim alive instead
tasks.description:
atm must not be able to run commands (the user's security decision, 2026-11-06): `atm run <id> -- <command>` (`loop run` in the new tree) goes. Today a permission prompt covers the whole line, but once `atm run *` is allowed, any command runs through it unchecked. What it gave, a claim kept alive during a long command (a test suite, a wait on CI), comes from a new `atm claim hold <id>` that runs nothing.

## `claim hold <id>`
- The agent writes `atm claim hold T-1 && npm test` in one Bash call. `claim hold` renews the claim once, starts a detached watcher and returns at once; the shell then runs the command itself. atm never sees it.
- The watcher follows the shell that called `claim hold` (its parent process): it renews the claim at the usual interval (three times per lease) while that process lives, and exits when it is gone. It checks the process's start time as well as its ID, so a reused ID doesn't keep it going.
- It stops after a cap (default 4 hours, `--max` to change it within bounds), and when the claim is released, finished or taken over. It renews only that claim, as that agent, and never fails loudly: an error ends the watcher, and the claim then lapses as usual.
- `--json` prints the claim and the watcher's PID and cap.

## Remove
`loop run` and its code (the child process, the renewal loop, exit-code passing), its tests, and its mentions in the skills (`do-task`, `loop-tasks`, `push`), `plugin/CLAUDE.md` and the docs (`docs/improving-atm-cli-ergonomics.md`, `docs/v4/atm-cli.md`, `docs/security-architecture.md`).

## Security
`docs/security-architecture.md`: atm runs no command an agent or a task text passes it, as an invariant with its check (a test that the command tree has no command taking a command to run). The watcher runs nothing and only writes claims; record it as such. Skills change, so the written skill review (§3.3).

## Tests
Scenarios or `claims.test.mjs`: `claim hold` renews while its parent lives and stops when it exits; it stops at the cap; it stops when the claim is released; a reused PID with another start time doesn't count. The changelog and What's new entries go with T-425's release.

notes.text: atm loop run removed; atm claim hold <id> (watcher follows the calling shell by pid+start time, --max 240 min). I24 + static check. Review: the watcher (cli/claims.py), skill wording.

tasks.name: Review decisions as their own commands; guarded exits from review; one skip
tasks.description:
Agreed with the user (2026-11-06). A review decision changes no state; the exits from review need the right decision. T-425 already moved approve and request-changes out of `task state` into `atm task review approve|request-changes <id>`; this finishes the model.

## Review decisions: `atm task review <decision> <id>`
The decision comes before the ID, so a permission prefix tells them apart.
- `approve <id> [--note]`, `review_state: approved`
- `request-changes <id> --reason`, `review_state: changes_requested`
- `reject <id> --reason`, `review_state: rejected` (new)

All three only on a task in review, and the task stays in review. **No skill pre-approves any of them:** they are the user's, and an agent asking for one gets a permission prompt the user answers.

## The exits from review, guarded in atm (`atm-cli/atm/lib/state.py`)
| Decision | Exit (`task state <id> …`) |
|---|---|
| `approved` | `done` |
| `changes_requested` | `in_progress` (its agent first, as now) |
| `rejected` | `todo` (back to the pool, the work dropped) or `skipped` |

Without the matching decision, atm refuses the exit, for an agent and a person alike: nobody passes, reworks or drops a review without the decision. The old `reject` transition (review to todo in one step) goes; `task state <id> todo` from review is the rejected exit.

## One skip
`skipped` from any open state (todo, blocked, in progress, in review; from review only once rejected), with `--resolution wont_do|obsolete|duplicate` and `--duplicate-of`; it releases the claim. `done` loses `--resolution`: done means the work is done.

## Update
- the skills (`do-task`, `loop-tasks`, `close-sprint`: an approval or a rejection is something the user runs, e.g. `! atm task review approve T-1`; no skill pre-approves `task review`), `plugin/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/task-states.md` (the diagram), `docs/improving-atm-cli-ergonomics.md`
- `docs/security-architecture.md`: I23 rests on atm's guards (the exits need the decision) and on no skill pre-approving `task review`; its check becomes the scenarios plus `skills.test.ts`
- the dashboard where it shows `review_state` (a `rejected` label)
- the skill review (§3.3), and the changelog with T-425's release

## Tests
Scenarios: each decision, refused outside review; each exit refused without its decision and allowed with it (an agent and a person); skip from each open state, from review only when rejected; done without `--resolution`. `skills.test.ts`: no skill pre-approves `task review`.

notes.text: task review approve|request-changes|reject; exits guarded in atm for everyone (done=approved, todo/skip=rejected, start=rework); skip from any open state; done has no --resolution. Review: state.py guards, cross-worktree record.

tasks.name: Claims renewed by atm itself, and a longer lease without hooks
tasks.description:

## Change
- Every atm command an agent runs renews that agent's live claims (as `atm claim heartbeat` does), under the lock it already takes. Reads renew too; a command run with `--agent` for someone else renews nothing.
- The default lease becomes 2 hours where nothing renews between commands, configurable in `meta` (a project that sets one keeps it). The plugin's hook keeps renewing as before; it becomes redundant, not wrong.
- `atm claim hold` is unchanged.
- `docs/v4/atm-cli.md`, the skills' and `plugin/CLAUDE.md`'s lines about leases, the changelog.

## Tests
Scenarios: a command renews the caller's claims and not another agent's; the default lease; `meta` overrides it. `pnpm run test:scripts` green.

notes.text: Every atm command renews the caller’s own claims (ten minutes on, as `heartbeat --auto`; not with `--agent`); default lease 2 h. Review: the review hand-back window grows to 2 h too; release 0.32.0 started (version bump).

## Change
- `atm-db`: the task folder's **lock** as the Python atm has it (`db/jsongit/lock.py`): a lock folder with `owner.json`, waited for up to `ATM_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, broken when its owner is dead or it is over a minute old, released on exit and on SIGTERM; the same folder, so the Python and the Rust atm can run against one project during the switch (`lock.test.mjs`, and `atm _lock-test`). `porting-to-rust.md` §3 says `std::fs::File::lock`: correct it to the lock folder.

- `atm-db`: the **change transaction** (`JsonGitStore.change`, `db/working.py`): under the lock, read `tasks.json` and the claims store, let the change run, write only what changed (`tasks.json` only when its text changed, with the archive first when tasks move into it), atomically, as `to_json` + newline.
- `atm-lib`: the change's actor and time (`ATM_NOW`, `ATM_AGENT` / the session) as later slices need them.

## Tests
Unit tests for the lock (two holders, a dead owner, an old lock, the timeout) and for writing only what changed; `lock.test.mjs` leaves `tests/scripts/rust-expected-failures.json`.

notes.text: The write path in Rust: the lock folder (Python’s protocol, SIGTERM-safe via `signal-hook`, owner checks via `sysinfo`), the claims store and its snapshot, the change transaction (`Store::change`, `Working`), `atm _lock-test`; `lock.test.mjs` passes (6 off the list); porting doc §3 corrected

tasks.description:

## What CI showed
- With atm's 10 s lock wait: agents time out waiting for the lock (`timed out waiting for the lock …/wt2/.agentic-task-manager/.lock`).
- With the test's lock wait raised to 60 s on Windows (decided with Hakan, `ATM_LOCK_TIMEOUT`): the test fails after 29 s, with the cleanup's `EPERM` on the test's folder, which hides the assertion underneath: some process still has the folder open.

## To find
- What still holds the folder: an atm process that outlives the test (a `claim hold` watcher not ending with its shell on Windows is a suspect: the same `EPERM` shows in `claims.test.mjs`'s watcher test), or a slow exit.
- Whether the lock is slow on Windows (git and process starts there are several times slower), and whether agents queue longer than they should.

## Done when
The test passes on CI's Windows runner, ideally at atm's default lock wait.

notes.text: Also on macOS CI, twice on 2026-11-08 (runs 42433227055 on `dev/0.33.0`, 42439602611 on `dev/0.32.0`), each passing on another run: agent-16 timed out on atm’s 10 s lock wait in `wt2`. So the lock queues too long under 16 agents on slow runners, not only on Windows.

The lock’s queue: the wait starts again when the lock changes hands (owner.json’s new token), up to 6× the wait; unit tests for both. The macOS CI timeout is this; the Windows run is checked in ATM-482 (the suite isn’t run on Windows CI until then), which also owns the EPERM (claim watcher).

tasks.name: The app's in-app updates (Tauri updater)
tasks.description:
The app checks for, downloads and installs its own updates through Tauri's updater plugin (agentic-status-bar, not a Tauri app, uses Sparkle: only its release habits carry over, not its mechanism).

## Change
- `tauri-plugin-updater`, its endpoint a `latest.json` update manifest attached to each GitHub release.
- The release workflow signs the app bundle with Tauri's updater key (a new secret, `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` and its password; separate from the Developer ID signature) and writes `latest.json`; the public key is built into the app.
- The app asks before installing; never updates silently. The bundled `atm` binary updates with it.
- A Homebrew cask install updates through `brew upgrade` instead (the cask says `auto_updates true`, or the updater is off for it: decide in the task).

## Docs
`packaging/README.md` (the secret, the manifest), `docs/security-architecture.md` (a new entry point: downloads and installs code).

tasks.name: Release 0.33.0: atm as the Rust CLI only
tasks.description:
The first release without the plugin: `dev/0.33.0` to `main`, tagged, built, signed and published, with the formula and the first export of the skills to `solo-swe/skills`. The release process is in [packaging/README.md](packaging/README.md).

## On `dev/0.33.0`
- **Version:** `0.33.0` in `Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.package]`), and `Cargo.lock` after `cargo build`.
- **CHANGELOG.md:** the `[Unreleased]` entries become `## [0.33.0] - <date>`: T-453, T-454, T-477, T-478, T-480, and how plugin users move.
- **WHATS-NEW.md:** a `## [0.33.0]` entry, 3–6 plain bullets of at most 180 characters each (`release-notes.test.ts`): atm is now its own program (Homebrew or a download), its skills go into your agents with one command, and your projects and dashboard carry over.

tasks.name: A release whose tasks merge in several PRs is never released
tasks.description:
`atm vcs pushed --pr <n>` releases a planned release only when **all** its tasks are merged **in that PR** (`release_with_merge` in [code.rs](crates/atm-lib/src/code.rs)). Release 0.32.0's sprint, *The Rust port*, merged in two PRs: #39 (32 tasks), then #40 (the other 5, which shipped in 0.33.0). Recording #39 said `0.32.0 stays planned: T-453, … are not merged in PR #39`, and recording #40 said the same about #39's 32 tasks. So 0.32.0 stays planned although every one of its tasks is merged.

## Change
- A release is released when every one of its tasks is merged (`merged_at` set), whichever PR merged it. Its release time is the last merge. The message names the tasks that keep it planned because they aren't merged yet, not because they merged in another PR.
- `atm vcs pushed` releases such a release the next time it runs. `atm doctor` (or `atm release list`) points out a planned release whose tasks are all merged, so this repo's 0.32.0 can be fixed by running it again.

## Tests
A scenario in `tests/scripts/scenarios/`: a release whose tasks are in two PRs stays planned after the first merge and is released by the second; a release with one PR still works as it does now.

notes.text: A release is released once all its tasks are merged, in any PR (released_at its last merge); messages say "not merged yet"; atm doctor warns about a planned release whose tasks are all merged. Scenarios in pr.json and releases.json. This repo’s 0.32.0 is released by `atm vcs pushed --pr 40` once this atm is installed.

tasks.name: Review and refactor the CI jobs from what the Rust port taught us
tasks.description:
Go through `.github/workflows/` with the user and propose changes, based on what CI did during *The Rust port* and the first releases. Each change is agreed first: editing CI is the user's call.

## What to look at
- **What runs when:** pushes to a release branch run nothing unless dispatched (`gh workflow run CI --ref <branch>`); a PR runs again after every push. Is that still the right trade?
- **Time and caching:** a run takes about 4–5 minutes. Look at the cargo and pnpm caches, the jobs that build the dashboard and atm more than once (Rust ×3, `atm for the e2e suite`, Playwright), and whether artifacts could be shared instead.
- **The app (T-455 onwards)** is part of `cargo build`/`test`, so the Linux job needs the webview's system packages and Windows builds against WebView2. See what that adds to each job, and whether the e2e binary and the release should build only `-p atm-cli`.
- **Windows:** the suite runs only partly there (T-480, T-482), and the stress test fails (T-481). Decide what the Windows job checks until those are done.
- **macOS:** the stress test hit lock timeouts twice (T-481). Is that a slow runner or a real bug?
- **Screenshots:** CI makes missing Linux baselines, and the local scripts get a Linux atm (T-485). Check that the two use the same binary and the same steps.
- **Runner images:** `ubuntu-latest` moves to Ubuntu 26 (CI's annotation); the e2e binary is built on 22.04 for an older glibc. Pin the images we depend on.
- **Required checks:** the ruleset names jobs by their display names (`Rust (ubuntu-latest)`, …), so renaming a job breaks merges. Keep the names in one place, or test that `.github/rulesets/main.json` matches `ci.yml` (`ci-workflow.test.ts`).
- **Release workflows:** `release.yml`, `homebrew.yml` and `skills.yml` worked first time for 0.32.0 and 0.33.0. Note anything worth keeping in `packaging/README.md`.

## Outcome
The agreed changes in the workflows, `ci-workflow.test.ts` and `AGENTS.md`'s CI section, with `docs/security-architecture.md` updated if a permission or secret changes.

Saved from main only, never in release.yml. → A: Swatinem/rust-cache.; cargo-deny in its own job, in parallel, and added to the required checks (§2.2)? → Yes: its own job, a required check.; Pin the runner images (ubuntu-24.04, macos-15, windows-2025) and rename the jobs Rust (Linux) / Rust (macOS) / Rust (Windows), you updating the live ruleset when it merges (§2.3)? → Yes: pin the images, name the jobs by platform; Hakan applies the ruleset.; CI on pushes to dev/** with cancel-in-progress, or keep dispatching by hand (§2.5)? → Trigger automatically: runs are free for open source, and atm is open source.; Screenshots: their own step, regenerated in the release task as now, or regenerated in the task that changes the UI (§2.7)? → A: the screenshots as their own step, regenerated in the release task.; A backlog task for the Linux build’s image (ubuntu-22.04 is retired around April 2027) (§2.6)? → A backlog task is fine.

tasks.name: Overhaul atm's human-readable output: alignment, grouping and styling
tasks.description:
atm's plain output (without `--json`) is hard to scan. For example, `atm project status` prints the per-sprint, per-type and per-label counts as one long comma-separated line each, and the blocked and waiting lists as long lines joined with `;`. Make it read well in a terminal without changing what it says or what `--json` returns.

## First, a design with the user
Propose the look before changing code: a before/after of `atm project status`, `atm task list`, `atm task details`, `atm sprint list`, `atm release list` and `atm doctor`. Decide:
- **Alignment:** columns padded to the widest value (IDs, statuses, priorities), long names cut or wrapped to the terminal's width, and sections with a heading and indented lines instead of `a, b, c` runs.
- **Styling:** bold headings, colour for status kinds and priorities, dimmed secondary text. Only when standard output is a terminal; never with `NO_COLOR`, `--json`, or output going to a pipe or file.
- **What `project status` leads with:** the active sprint and what's next first; the long breakdowns (all sprints, types, labels) shorter, or behind a flag.
- **Dependencies:** terminal width and colour either hand-written or from a crate (e.g. `anstyle`, already in the tree through clap). Any new crate is proposed first.

## Agents read this output too
The skills relay what atm prints, and agents act on it. Keep it plain text when it isn't a terminal, keep each fact on a line agents can find, and check `docs/agent/` and the skills that quote output. A change to output agents act on follows AGENTS.md's security checklist (the written review in `docs/security-architecture.md` §3.3).

## Tests
The scenarios' exact `stdout` expectations change with the new layout: update them in one place per command. Add a test that a pipe gets no escape codes and that `NO_COLOR` turns colour off.

tasks.name: ADR-003: workspaces, the set of projects atm works on
tasks.description:
A design proposal, as an ADR, for a **workspace**: a set of projects atm works on, of which there may be several (usually one; others for tests, or work and personal projects).

## Why
The logic that works across projects (the project list with summaries, worktrees and logos; search across projects; skipping a broken project) lives in atm-api's HTTP routes, and the app (T-456) needs the same. atm-lib knows only one project; the registry is concrete in atm-db; boot is a bag of openers and JSON-in-git helpers ([layered-architecture.md](docs/layered-architecture.md) §3.2, §5.1, §11.2).

## The ADR
- Research: how atm's layers handle one project and many today; what the registry, `ATM_HOME`, `atm service`, the dashboard's routes and the app assume; how other tools model workspaces.
- Propose the workspace: what it is and holds, how one is chosen (default, `ATM_HOME`, a flag), the API's place for it (`api/v<N>/workspace/…`), the layers that own it, and how boot gets simpler.
- Diagrams in Mermaid. Options with trade-offs, a recommendation, consequences and a migration plan.

Reviewed with Hakan; T-456 waits for it.

notes.text: ADR-003 drafted (docs/adr/ADR-003-workspaces.md): workspaces as named lists over the home’s project index, chosen per call (flag > env > stored default), atm-lib’s Workspace with a ProjectOpener, boot as the composition root, api/v2/workspaces/<w>/…, a migration plan. Four questions for the review at the end.
Approved: Approved in Crit after one round (the task folder is the store’s, not the model’s)

ADR-003 accepted: workspaces in the state folder (platform app data, ATM_STATE_DIR), no project index, no boot (settings file + factories in atm-db and atm-vcs), atm workspace commands, api/v2/workspaces, a six-step migration.

Mermaid diagrams in the app need it (T-502).

## Steps (§4.7)
1. **A check first, in a branch:** the plugin's smallest form, in `cargo run -p atm-app` and `cargo tauri dev`. Does WebKit let the opaque-origin frame load modules from `compmd://localhost` with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`? Does Tauri leave the scheme's responses alone? 2. **Decide with Hakan (§4.6):** the plugin as a crate of its own in atm's workspace (`crates/tauri-plugin-compmd/`, no atm dependencies) until CompMD ships one.
3. **The change (§4.1, §4.2):** the plugin (embedded folder, path checks, H1/H2 headers, 404/405 with reasons); the app's CSP names `compmd://localhost` and `http://compmd.localhost`, `frame-ancestors 'none'` back, `devCsp` only adds the CLI's socket; the dashboard gives CompMD a full `base` in the app (`convertFileSrc('', 'compmd')`).
4. **Nothing fails silently (§4.3):** `CompMd.svelte` listens for the view's `error` event and shows a note at the block; a failed `compmd.js` load shows a note on the text; both log the cause.

## Tests (§4.5)
The plugin's handler; the app's policy; no IPC from `compmd:`; atm serve and the plugin on the same header table; the page's error notes; by hand in a window, both `cargo tauri dev` and `cargo run -p atm-app`, with T-502's test diagrams and Help.

tasks.name: CompMD's files from compmd:// after an upgrade: WebKit's custom-scheme cache
tasks.description:
A gap in [ADR-004](docs/adr/ADR-004-compmd-in-tauri-through-its-own-protocol.md): WebKit (WKWebView, on macOS and iOS) caches a custom URI scheme's responses, so a file replaced at the same path can keep running its old version (seen in another Tauri app's custom-scheme frames). ADR-004 keeps the paths CompMD's files have under `atm serve` (`/assets/compmd/<version>/…`). The CompMD version in the path changes with CompMD, but not when atm rebuilds the same CompMD version differently (its packs, `compmd.config.json`, a pack's built module), so after an atm upgrade the app could run the previous files from `compmd://`, and the page and its frames could speak different versions of the frame protocol.

## 1. Check it first
In the running app on macOS (`cargo run -p atm-app`, and a bundle): open a task with a diagram; replace a CompMD file the plugin serves (a frame's `runtime.js`, or the Mermaid pack's module) with a changed copy at the same path, one that shows it changed (a console line); rebuild, run again, open the task: does the old file still run? Record what each build showed.

## 2. If it does, fix it in `tauri-plugin-compmd`, as the plugin's default
The plugin is meant to move into CompMD for any Tauri host (ADR-004 decision 5), so the fix is its default behaviour, not atm's configuration. One of:
- **Content-hashed paths:** the plugin serves the build's CompMD folder under a name made from a hash of its files, gives the page that `base` (H4), and answers with `Cache-Control: max-age=31536000, immutable`; a changed file is then a new path;
- **or, if the paths must stay as under `atm serve`:** `Cache-Control: no-cache` with a validator (an `ETag` and `If-None-Match`, as `atm serve` sends) that WebKit honours for custom schemes; check in the app that it does.
Prefer the first if WebKit's handling of validators on custom schemes is uncertain.

## 3. Record it
- ADR-004: the result in its Risks; a decision if the plugin changes (and the design doc's §4.2 if its headers change).
- The plugin's header tests stay in step with `atm serve`'s (H1, H2: CORS `*`, `nosniff`, `sandbox allow-scripts` on frame documents); if the cache headers differ between the two, say why in both.

notes.text: Scope after T-503 (ADR-005): the frames are CompMD’s plugin’s, at content-hashed paths, so the cache can’t serve an old frame. What is left to check is atm’s own atm: scheme (assets.rs: compmd.js, its WebAssembly, the packs’ modules, at /assets/compmd/<version>/, no-cache). A stale pack module fails its hash check visibly; check compmd.js across a rebuild of the same CompMD version, and if it sticks, name the folder by a hash.

Checked on macOS 26: two app builds with different compmd.js at the same atm: path each ran their own, so WebKit doesn’t cache atm: responses (no-cache honoured) and the paths stay; recorded in ADR-005 Risks. Found and fixed on the way: the pack’s module was fetched from the page origin (tauri://), refused by connect-src; moduleUrl puts it on atm:.

`dev/0.35.0` to `main`, tagged, built, signed and published. The process is in [packaging/README.md](packaging/README.md); the last one was T-509.

## On `dev/0.35.0`
- **Version:** `0.35.0` in `Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.package]`), and `Cargo.lock` after `cargo build`.
- **CHANGELOG.md:** the `[Unreleased]` entries become `## [0.35.0] - <date>`; check they say what shipped (T-503 diagrams in the app with CompMD 0.6.0, T-506, T-483, T-508; T-510's design).

New entry points this release (the updater, which downloads and installs code; the app's subscription commands; the `atm:` scheme) are in the doc: check they describe what shipped.
- **Checks:** `pnpm run verify` in `dashboard/`; `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo deny check` from the root.

## The PR
- Open it with `/atm-push`: `dev/0.35.0` to `main`. The required checks must pass.
- The user merges it, or says to merge it. Then record the merge (`atm vcs pushed --pr <n> --at <mergedAt>`).

- `packaging/release.sh 0.35.0 --push` on an up-to-date `main`; watch the Release run. **The updater's artifacts are made for the first time** (the signed `.app.tar.gz` and `latest.json`): if the job fails, fix it on a branch and tag again, never by hand.

- Watch the Homebrew and Skills workflows (formula, cask with `auto_updates true`, skills `atm-v0.35.0`).

- **The page's side** (`dashboard/src/lib/compmd.ts`: `sandboxOptions`, `fetchPackModules`, `moduleUrl`): the frames' `base`, the packs' modules handed over as code checked by their `integrity`. Is this still the recommended way, or does CompMD's API cover it now?
