Where atm differs from the standard: change it (or record why not), keeping `atm serve` and the app serving the same files with the same headers (`tests/scripts/compmd-host-headers.json`). Update [ADR-005](docs/adr/ADR-005-compmds-tauri-plugin-and-atms-asset-scheme.md) (or a new ADR replacing it), I26, and the [Tauri guide](docs/guides/tauri.md). New dependencies or plugin versions need a yes first.

tasks.name: Design: two task IDs (a UUID and a project key, ATM-123) and dependencies across projects
tasks.description:
Hakan wants tasks to have two IDs, as JIRA does: a **UUID** for technical reasons, and a **key** for people, a project prefix and a number instead of `T-`: `ASB-001` (Agentic Status Bar), `ATM-001` (Agentic Task Manager), `FIG-001` (Fig), `LFB-001` (Learn Forever Blog). Keys let a task refer to another project's: `LFB-005` blocked by `ATM-978`.

Design it with Hakan, as an ADR replacing the current ID scheme (`docs/adr/`), then break the work into tasks with `/atm-create-tasks`.

## To settle
- **The two IDs:** `uid` (a UUID, never shown, never changed) and the key (`ATM-978`); the prefix in `meta` (e.g. `meta.key`), chosen at `atm db init`, unique across the workspace's projects; keys unique within the project. Which one the files, the API, the app's commands and the dashboard's addresses use.
- **Migration:** `atm db migrate` gives each task a UUID and rekeys `T-527` as `ATM-527`, keeping the numbers; dependencies, `related`, notes, commit trailers, PR records and links follow. Old IDs stay resolvable as aliases (commit messages and PRs say `T-527`). The archive too.
- **Merges and parallel agents:** the merge driver matches tasks by UUID; two branches that both add a task never collide, and the key of one is renumbered on merge (as today's driver renumbers).
- **Across projects:** a dependency or `related` entry naming another project's key, resolved through the workspace's projects (`projects.json`): its status shown, an unfinished one an unmet dependency for the loop; a project missing, renamed or rekeyed; the dashboard's link to it; `atm doctor`'s checks. Reading another project's task folder is a new entry point (`docs/security-architecture.md`).
- **Where IDs show:** the CLI and `atm docs`, the dashboard (cards, links, the graph, addresses), the app, commit templates and `atm vcs` parsing (`code.rs`'s mention of a task ID), the skills.

## Output
The ADR, reviewed with Hakan, and the implementation tasks (data model, migrate, merge driver, cross-project resolution, dashboard, docs, skills), added through `/atm-create-tasks`.

tasks.name: Task keys: the migration (atm db migrate) and atm project key set
tasks.description:
ADR-007 §6.

## The first migration (`atm db migrate`)
Every task, archived ones too: a UUID, its number from the ID's trailing digits (an ID that doesn't fit the file's prefix gets the next free number and keeps its old ID as an alias), references rewritten to UUIDs (`dependencies`, `related`, notes pointing at a task, claims keyed by UUID), `meta.key` from the name's initials when they make 3 to 6 letters (else the old prefix), the old prefix into `meta.key_history`, every task final, the format version set. Sets `meta.key`, pushes the old one onto `meta.key_history`; numbers and references unchanged. Warns (doesn't refuse) when another project in the user's workspaces uses the key. `atm db init` asks for a key on a new project, suggesting the initials.

Also ADR-007 §2/§6 give TaskMan as an example, which is 7 letters, over the 3–6 rule: fix the example.

tasks.name: The app: external links (About, Help, repository, PRs) open in the browser
tasks.description:
In the atm app, clicking a link in the About dialog does nothing (Hakan, 2026-11-16). The page's external links are plain `<a href target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">` anchors, which the app's webview doesn't open, and the app has no command or plugin that opens a link in the user's browser. So most likely **every** external link in the app is dead, not only the About dialog's: check each place first and list them in the outcome.

## Where the links are
`dialogs/AboutDialog.svelte` (source, CompMD), `ui/RepoRef.svelte` (commits, PRs), `overview/ProjectCard.svelte`, `kanban/KanbanColumns.svelte`, `progress/ReleaseView.svelte`, `shell/Footer.svelte`, `shell/ProjectTab.svelte`, `dialogs/WhatsNew.svelte`, `documents/DocumentViewer.svelte`, Help's links (rendered by CompMD: `docs/help.md`), and the Help ▸ CompMD menu item (`menu-actions.ts`, `page.open`).

## Change
- **One way to open an external link in the app**: the page hands `https:` (and `mailto:`) links to the app, which opens them in the system's browser; in the browser nothing changes. Prefer one place that catches every such link (a click handler on the document for external anchors, and `page.open`) over editing each component.
- **How the app opens them** is a choice to make first: Tauri's opener plugin (`tauri-plugin-opener`) is a **new dependency and needs Hakan's yes** before it is added (docs/guides/tauri.md, Platform features); the alternative is a small command of the app's own. Propose, don't add.
- **Only web addresses**: the app checks the URL itself (scheme `https`/`http`/`mailto` only, no `file:`, no custom schemes, no `atm:`), never trusts the page's; the capability allows only that command. Links inside rendered task text arrive from CompMD's sandbox as `link` events (compmd-rendering-design.md): they go through the same check.
- `docs/security-architecture.md`: opening a URL from the page is a new entry point (what is allowed, who checks it). `docs/guides/tauri.md` says how links open.

## Tests
Unit: the page sends external links to the app and keeps internal ones (`/projects/…`, `#…`) in the page; the app's check refuses other schemes (Rust test). e2e under `asApp()`: clicking the About dialog's source link and a commit link calls the app's command with the URL; in the browser the anchor stays `target="_blank"`. Then check by hand in a window (`cargo run -p atm-app`): About, Help ▸ CompMD, a PR link.

notes.text: Decided (Hakan, 2026-11-16): use Tauri’s opener plugin (`tauri-plugin-opener`), approved as a new dependency; pin it to a release at least two weeks old, as the other Tauri plugins are

External links in the app go through one command, `open_url` (app/src-tauri/src/external.rs): https/http with a host or mailto only, else refused; opened with `tauri-plugin-opener` =2.7.2 from Rust, the page has no opener permission. One capture handler in the layout catches every anchor; `page.open` too. Not checked in a real window: try About, Help ▸ CompMD and a PR link

tasks.name: ADR-008: other projects' tasks, referenced from any registered project and loaded when needed (replaces ADR-007 §7's wording)
tasks.description:
Write `docs/adr/ADR-008-…md` from [the freshness design](docs/cross-project-freshness-design.md) §4.1 (K4) and §9, as AGENTS.md asks for a decision that changes an ADR.

## What it decides
- **Any registered project** can be referenced, written by key or UUID; a key is looked up among every registered project, not only those of the workspaces the referring project is in (ADR-007 §7 said the latter; the code, `foreign::registered`, already does the former).
- **Loaded when needed, never watched:** another project is read when something needs it (readiness, display), through the stamp-keyed cache (design §5.1 B); only the open workspace's own projects are watched, for the app.
- **Worktree branches** (design §4.2): another project counts as its main working copy (V1).
- **The browser polls; the app is pushed** (design 1), and the store owns how it hears of changes (design §3).

## Also
ADR-007 gets a line under its status: "§7's lookup and freshness replaced by ADR-008". Link the design from both.

notes.text: ADR-008 written (any registered project referable, loaded when needed, never watched; the browser polls, the app is pushed; the store owns how it hears of changes; another project as its main copy). ADR-007 and the design point to it

tasks.name: Other projects' tasks: one stamp-keyed cache for the rules and the display
tasks.description:
[The freshness design](docs/cross-project-freshness-design.md) §5.1, option **B**: fixes P1, P4 and P5.

## The bug
`foreign::status` (the `ForeignStatus` hook the rules use: `waiting_for`, `ready`, unmet dependencies, the summary's `next` and board cards) remembers each answer for the whole process (`static SEEN`), so in `atm serve` and the app a task keeps reading "waiting on ATM-1" after ATM-1 is done, until a restart, while `derived.foreign` (T-549) shows it done and `atm loop next` takes it.

## Change (`crates/atm-lib/src/foreign.rs`)
- **One cache for the rules and the display**, keyed by the other project's `meta.id`: the project, its document and archive as read, and its store's `stamp()` (`tasks`, `archive`).
- **On each use**, compare the store's current stamp: unchanged → use the entry; changed → read the project again. Entries also **expire after a few seconds** (a constant, e.g. 5 s), against coarse file timestamps.
- `status`, `label`, `Lookup::view`, `find_uuid` and `resolve_in_other_project` all read through it; `registered()` is no longer opened per reference.
- The registry (which projects are registered, and where) is part of the key: a project removed from the workspaces, or its folder gone, is seen on the next use.
- Thread-safe (the server's threads): a `Mutex`, never held while reading a project.

## Tests
- **atm-lib:** in one process (no restart), after the other project's task is marked done, `status` and `Lookup::view` both say done, and a task depending on it is ready; an unchanged stamp doesn't re-read (count the reads); the entry expires; a removed project is `unregistered`.
- **The CLI suite (`serve.test.mjs`):** with a running `atm serve`, two registered projects: the other's task done → A's tasks route (without validators) gives `ready` true and no `waiting_for`; the overview's `next` follows.
- **The app (Rust command tests):** `project_tasks` within one `AppState` follows the other project's change.

notes.text: One cache for the rules and the display (`foreign.rs`), by registered folder, checked against the store’s `tasks`/`archive` stamp, 5 s expiry; the registry cached by its workspace files’ stamps; no lock held while reading. The workspace summary follows the projects it depends on. A long-running `atm serve` now shows another project’s done task as ready, without a restart. No app test (another agent had the app): it calls the same atm-lib

tasks.name: The tasks route's ETag also covers the projects a project's tasks reference
tasks.description:
[The freshness design](docs/cross-project-freshness-design.md) §5.3, option **D**: fixes P2 (the browser's stale 304).

## The bug
`api_tasks` (`crates/atm-api/src/routes.rs`) builds its ETag from the project's own `tasks` and `archive` stamps and the query. When only a referenced project changes, the browser's poll gets a 304 and keeps the old status, `ready` and `waiting_for`.

## Change
- **Which projects A references** (the `meta.id`s in its tasks' `dependencies`, `related` and `duplicate_of`, the archive too) is worked out on a full read and remembered by the server **keyed by A's stamp, never by time** (a new reference changes A's stamp, so it is never missed). atm-lib gives it (e.g. `Member::referenced_projects()`), atm-api only uses it.
- **The ETag** becomes A's stamp, the query, and the referenced projects' `tasks` and `archive` stamps (a project not found counts as null, so it appearing or going changes the tag too).
- A project with no references costs nothing extra; one with some costs a stamp per referenced project per poll.
- `docs/multi-project-api.md`: the tasks route's ETag; drop the note T-549 added that another project's change shows only once this one changes.

## Tests
The CLI suite (`serve.test.mjs`): A references B; a conditional GET of A's tasks after B's task changes is a **200** with the new values; after a change in an unrelated project C, still a **304**; with nothing changed, a 304; a new reference added to A then B changing: a 200. e2e (`keys.spec.ts`, the real binary's views): the browser's poll (`page.clock`) shows the other project's task done.

notes.text: The tasks route’s ETag (and the overview’s) also covers the task data of the projects named in `dependencies`, `related`, `duplicate_of` (archive too; `foreign::named_by`, worked out once per stamp of the project’s own data). A poll sees a named project’s change; an unrelated change stays a 304 (serve.test.mjs). No e2e: the fixture server has no ETags of atm’s

tasks.name: Store::subscribe in atm-db: how a store hears of changes is the store's; the app's file watcher moves behind it
tasks.description:
[The freshness design](docs/cross-project-freshness-design.md) §3 and §5.5, option **L** (P6): watching for changes is the store's job, behind the abstraction, so a store that isn't files (a `JiraStore`) works the same.

## Change
- **atm-db's `Store` trait:** `subscribe(on_change) -> Subscription` (dropping it ends it), replacing `watch_folders()`. Its documentation says `on_change` runs on the store's own thread, and that every store must push or poll.
- **`JsonGitStore`:** watches its own folders (the task folder, the claims store, the working copies' task files) with `notify` and its debouncer, settled 300 ms, the code now in the app (`app/src-tauri/src/commands.rs`, `AppState::watch`). `notify` and `notify-debouncer-full` move from the app to atm-db (same versions, already approved; no new dependency).
- **`MemoryStore`:** told by its own writes.
- **`poll_stamp(store, interval, on_change)`** in atm-db: a helper an implementation may use when it can't push (none needs it yet: test it on its own). No polling default in the trait (Hakan, round 1).
- **The registry** (`workspaces/<w>.json`): a subscription for "the list changed".
- **atm-lib:** a workspace's changes are its members' subscriptions merged, plus the registry's; the app's `subscribe_workspace` and `subscribe_project` use that. Nothing above atm-db names a folder to watch.
- Behaviour unchanged for the user: the app is told of the same changes as now (the open workspace's own projects); the browser polls.
- `docs/layered-architecture.md` and `docs/guides/tauri.md` (Streams) say where watching lives.

## Tests
atm-db: the JSON store's subscription tells a change in its task file and its claims and stops when dropped; `poll_stamp` tells a stamp change; the memory store tells its writes. atm-lib: a workspace subscription merges its members' and the registry's. The app's existing subscription tests (`a_subscription_says_when_a_watched_folder_changes…`, `a_window_loading_again…`) pass unchanged.

notes.text: `Store::subscribe(on_change)` in atm-db replaces `watch_folders`: the JSON store watches its own folders (notify, moved from the app), the memory store tells its writes, `poll_stamp` for stores that poll; the registry subscribes to the workspaces folder; atm-lib merges them (`Workspace::subscribe`, `Member::subscribe`). The app’s messages are the same; a burst touching two projects may now send two

## Tests
`tests/scripts/output.test.mjs` "task text can’t drive the terminal".

notes.text: output::clean drops task text’s control characters before the terminal (I30); --json exact. Found in 0.38.0’s security review of T-488; the CLI suite (647) passes.

tasks.name: Flaky on Linux CI: the app test the_page_is_served_with_a_policy_it_works_under once didn’t find the page in the app’s files
tasks.description:
On PR #51 (0.38.0), CI run 43990284864's `Rust (ubuntu-latest)` failed `app/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`'s `the_page_is_served_with_a_policy_it_works_under` with "the dashboard's page in the app's files" (the asset resolver had no `tasks-dashboard.html`); the same code passed on the run before and on the re-run, and on macOS and Windows. The dashboard had been built before `cargo test` (`pnpm run build`).

## To find
Why the mock app's asset resolver can miss the page: another test in the same process changing what the context embeds or reads (the tests run in parallel threads; `context()` is generated per call), Tauri reading assets from disk in debug builds while something rewrites `dashboard/dist/`, or the build order in CI's job. Reproduce in the Linux container if needed.

## Done when
The cause is found and fixed (or the test made independent of it), without retrying or skipping the test.

notes.text: Cause (from tauri-codegen 2.7.4’s source): `generate_context!` writes each compressed asset to OUT_DIR/tauri-codegen-assets/<hash>.<ext> only if it doesn’t exist, in place. `cargo test`/`clippy --all-targets` expand it twice at once (the lib, and the lib’s tests): the second can embed the 736 KB page half-written, so it doesn’t decompress and `get` gives None. Fix needs a build dependency or a CI change.

Fix A: pre-fill Tauri’s asset cache from app/src-tauri/build.rs (one `tauri_codegen::context_codegen` call with the app’s config, before either compile), adding `tauri-codegen` (already in Cargo.lock through Tauri) as a direct build-dependency. Fix B: in ci.yml, run `cargo build --locked` before clippy and test, so one compile fills the cache. tasks.name: Code review: the atm-review crate, its model and the ReviewStore trait
tasks.description:
Phase 1 of [the code review design](docs/code-review-design.md) (approved 2026-11-17).

## Change
- A new crate `crates/atm-review`, depending on `atm-common` and `atm-vcs` only (not atm-db, not the task model: a task is a key string).
- The model: `Review` (header, summary, chains, rounds), statuses `draft`, `open`, `live`, `changes_requested`, `approved`, `closed` ([§3.2](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.2%20A%20review%20and%20how%20it%20goes)), `Round` (kinds `range`, `working`, `files`, and live checkpoints), `Chain`, `Comment` (top-level ones with `resolved`, replies nested, [§3.4](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.4%20Comments)), `Anchor`, `ReviewId` and `ReviewRef`.
- The `ReviewStore` trait with one method per operation ([§3.10](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.10%20The%20store)), and an in-memory store for the tests.
- The rules above the store: approve only when every top-level comment is resolved; who may resolve; the status changes of the state diagram.
- `tests/scripts/layers.test.mjs` gains the crate, and checks it depends on neither atm-db nor atm-lib.

## Tests
Unit tests of the rules on the memory store.

notes.text: crates/atm-review: the model (reviews, statuses, rounds, chains with nested replies, anchors), the ReviewStore trait (one method per operation), the rules (who may resolve, decide, approve only when every top-level comment is resolved, the state diagram) and a memory store; 10 tests. OnChange/Subscription moved to atm-common so both stores share them; layers.test.mjs has the crate.

tasks.name: Code review: comments.md and review.md, written and read back

Round trips of both files, the example in §3.4, a hand-broken file kept and reported.

tasks.name: Code review: the file store (folders, numbers, locks, subscriptions, worktrees)

tasks.name: Code review: rounds from a range, uncommitted changes or files, compared and anchored
tasks.description:
Rounds and anchors ([§3.3](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.3%20The%20records), [§3.6](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.6%20Rounds%2C%20anchors%20and%20drift)), through `atm-vcs`.

## Change
- A round's diff from a commit range, the working tree against its base (uncommitted changes, live checkpoints), or files as they are (as if added); `git diff -M`, three lines of context; binary files listed with their blob IDs, never copied; deleted files as a line.
- No snapshots: two rounds compared by rebuilding each round's files from its base and diff on a temporary index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `git apply --cached`, `git write-tree`), never touching the user's index or working tree.
- Anchors moved from the round they were made on to a later one through the change between them; a chain whose quote is gone is drifted, at its last place, with the round and lines it was made on.

## Tests
Rounds of each kind, two uncommitted rounds compared, an anchor moved and one drifted, the user's index unchanged.

notes.text: atm-vcs diff.rs: a range’s diff, the working tree’s (temporary index, new files in, the user’s index untouched), files as added, a round’s tree rebuilt from base+patch, trees compared. atm-review rounds.rs: rounds of each kind, compare (no snapshots), anchors followed line by line through hunks (kept, found again by quote, or drifted with where made). 10 tests; I24’s list has the new git starts.

tasks.name: Code review: the task link (reviews on tasks, decisions to tasks, live approval)
tasks.description:

## Change

- Tasks named when a review is created, when a live review starts, or later (add, remove), with what each does to the task's status ([§3.2](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.2%20A%20review%20and%20how%20it%20goes)).
- A reviewer's submit becomes every named task's review decision (approve, request changes with a `rejection` note linking the review); closing rejects only when the user says so. Decisions stay the user's (I23).
- A live review's approval is the task's when the task's change hasn't moved since the approved checkpoint; otherwise what changed is said ([§3.5](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.5%20Live%20reviews)).

## Tests
Scenarios (`tests/scripts/scenarios/`): a task through a review and a round, a batch review of two tasks, a live approval with and without a change since.

notes.text: atm-lib reviews.rs: create/add_round/submit/close/set_tasks keep the tasks in step (code_reviews links by UUID+ref; open review puts tasks in review; a decision is every named task’s, as the reviewer); apply_live_approval approves a task whose working diff equals the approved live checkpoint. tasks.name: Tests: every case, not a coverage number (scan the repo)
tasks.description:
Scan the whole repository's tests against the model in [AGENTS.md, Testing conventions](AGENTS.md#:~:text=What%20to%20test), and add or update tests where cases are missing.

## The model
- **Every case.** Each unit's tests cover every case it promises, not just the lines that run: the happy paths, each failure mode and refusal, each class of input (empty, one, many; missing, malformed, too large; at and past each limit), each state, and where two of these meet. The coverage thresholds stay as guardrails. Use judgement to keep the tests maintainable: one test per behaviour, tables of cases, shared fixtures, and each layer tests its own rules.
- **A unit alone.** A unit test replaces what it calls in another layer with a hand-written fake behind a trait (a stub of the module or API in TypeScript), and checks the unit's own work. Going through the layers together is the integration tests' job: a crate's `tests/`, `tests/scripts/`, e2e. Unit tests that go through the layers below today (real git, a real store, the disk) either move to integration tests or get a fake.
- **The example:** `crates/atm-api/src/routes/`, done in ATM-572. Its seam is `source.rs` (the traits, with atm-lib's implementation), its fake is `test_support.rs` (records each call and answers what a test sets), and each module's tests cover each class of answer.

## The known gap
**Claims** (`crates/atm-lib/src/claims.rs`, `claims/tests.rs`, `leases.rs`, `crates/atm-db/src/jsongit/claims.rs`, `memory.rs`): the Rust tests cover the heartbeat and expiry only. Missing:
- a free task is claimed;
- a task claimed by another agent is refused;
- a task is refused from another worktree or branch of the same project;
- the holder claims its own task again;
- release, and claiming after a release;
- an expired lease is taken over.

Some of these are checked end to end in `tests/scripts/claims.test.mjs`, but not in the layer that owns the rule. atm-lib's tests already use `MemoryStore` as the store's fake.

## The scan
Go crate by crate, then the app and the dashboard. List each unit's cases next to its tests, fill the gaps, and replace the layers below with fakes where a unit test goes through them:
- [ ] `atm-common`, `atm-fs`, `atm-vcs`, `atm-db` (the stores, the merge driver, the registry)
- [ ] `atm-docs`, `atm-review`
- [ ] `atm-lib` (claims, leases, the status machine, sprints, reviews, workspaces, query)
- [ ] `atm-cli` (each command's refusals and exit codes) and `tests/scripts/`
- [ ] `app/src-tauri` (each command's results and refusals; its tests that read a real project are integration tests)
- [ ] `dashboard/` (unit and component tests: API errors, 304s, empty data)

Record in the task's outcome note what was added per area, and anything left out on purpose, with the reason.

notes.text: Rust 432 to 837 tests, CLI suite 663 to 814, dashboard unit 1567 to 1635 (96.5% lines). Claims in atm-lib (MemoryStore::with_here). Left out: a trait in front of Workspaces in the app and GitVcs in atm-docs (refactors), proptest (a dependency), state.svelte.ts. 10 known bugs are todo tests (empty folder left, review cmds without a task file); unarchive of a duplicated ID, agents --dry-run.

tasks.name: Code review: reviews of changes that touch submodules
tasks.description:
atm code reviews fail for submodule commits (Hakan, 2026-11-18). A project with submodules must be reviewable like any other.

## Reproduce first
In a test repository with a submodule, try each and note what fails and where (`atm review create`, `atm review round`, `atm review show`, the review page):
1. **A range that moves a submodule's commit** in the superproject: git diffs a gitlink (mode `160000`) as `Subproject commit <old>` / `<new>`, with no file contents. The round's diff, its tree (`tree_after`, `diff_trees`, `file_in` in `crates/atm-vcs/src/diff.rs`) and the anchoring in `crates/atm-review/src/rounds.rs` likely don't expect it.
2. **Commits made inside the submodule**: the range is in the submodule's repository, not the superproject's.
3. **Uncommitted changes** with a submodule that is dirty or has new commits, and `--file` on a path inside a submodule.

## Change
- A moved submodule shows in the round as one entry: its path, the old and new commits (short SHAs, linked to the submodule's repository when it has a web address, as `submodule_of` in `crates/atm-vcs/src/lib.rs` gives the document viewer), with no lines to comment on but a comment on the entry as a whole.
- A review of changes inside a submodule: decide with the reproduction whether `atm review create` run in the submodule (or `--range` naming it) reviews the submodule's own commits, its files shown under the submodule's path; files in a submodule read from the submodule's repository at the round's commit (as the document viewer already does).
- Nothing fails silently: what isn't supported says so (e.g. a nested submodule's range), with the exit code and a message saying what to do.
- The dashboard's diff viewer shows a submodule entry (`dashboard/src/lib/reviews/`).

## Tests
atm-vcs unit tests on a repository with a submodule (the diff, the tree, a gitlink in the patch); atm-review tests for a round with a submodule entry and a comment on it; a CLI suite test in `tests/scripts/reviews.test.mjs` (create, round, show with a submodule moved and with commits inside it); a component or e2e test for the submodule entry in the diff viewer.

notes.text: Submodules reviewable: atm in a submodule finds the project; rounds of a submodule's commits (Round.submodule) show its files under its path; a moved submodule is one entry with its commits, commentable as a whole. Not here: atm vcs commit of files in a submodule (git refuses from the project).

tasks.name: App: menu → Reload leaves an empty window with an error in the title bar
tasks.description:
In the atm app, choosing **Reload** in the menu (⌘R) leaves the window empty, with an error showing in the title bar (Hakan, 2026-11-18). Reload should show the same page again, as it was.

## Reproduce first
Open a project's page (and a review in its tab, a task's details, a document), choose Reload; note the address, what the window shows, the title bar's text and the web inspector's console. Try it on the root page too.

## Likely cause
The menu's `reload` action runs `location.reload()` ([`menu-actions.ts`](dashboard/src/lib/menu-actions.ts#L48)). The page's addresses are its routes (`/projects/<id>/list`, `…/reviews/CR-7`), and the app's window serves the built dashboard as one HTML file: a reload asks the app for the route's path itself, which it has no file for, unless it falls back to the page. Check how the app serves the page (`app/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, `assets.rs`, `tauri.conf.json`) and how the title bar shows a load error (`AppTitleBar.svelte`).

## Change
Make Reload show the page again at the same address, with its tabs: either the app answers every page route with the dashboard (as `atm serve`'s `PAGE_PATH` does, `docs/multi-project-api.md` §2.7; never for asset or API paths), or the page reloads through the app's root with the address handed over. Whatever made the title bar show an error says what went wrong in words, if it can still happen.

## Tests
An e2e test in `dashboard/tests/e2e/app.spec.ts`: Reload on a project's tab, a review's tab and the root shows the same page and tabs, no error in the title bar; a unit test in the app for the route fallback if that's the fix (asset and unknown paths still 404).

notes.text: Reload in the app goes through a new reload_window command: the window comes back with its tabs at the app page. Untested on a real app window: try menu Reload (Cmd+R) on a project tab and a review tab.

tasks.name: Code review: the Diffs tab loads slowly for long diffs (proposals, then the fix)
tasks.description:
A review with a long diff takes a long time before its Diffs tab shows (Hakan, 2026-11-18). Find where the time goes, propose ways to make it fast, decide with Hakan, then do it.

## Measure first
A review of a few thousand changed lines (one large file, and many files) in the browser and the app: the time to the first file drawn and to the tab settled, split into atm's answer (`review_page` in [`review_pages.rs`](crates/atm-lib/src/review_pages.rs): the round's patch, trees rebuilt with `git apply`, every chain placed with a tree diff each, `rounds::place`), the transfer, and the page (parsing every file's patch, `diff.ts`; the file cards, `ReviewFile.svelte`, `DiffView.svelte`, the sides' documents loaded per file). `tests/e2e/performance.spec.ts` has the review budget to extend (*review file far down*).

## Proposals to weigh (write them up, with numbers)
- **Paging the files:** the page asks for the round's file list first (paths, statuses, counts), and each file's patch and sides when its card nears the view (`?file=` on the review route), so a review of hundreds of files sends what is looked at.
- **Paging inside a file:** a very long file's diff drawn in chunks (its hunks, a few hundred rows at a time) as it scrolls, its rows virtualised.
- **atm's side:** trees rebuilt once per round and cached (by round and patch hash), chains placed in one tree diff per file instead of one per chain, the answer cached by the review's stamp (ETag/304 as the task routes do).
- **The page:** patches parsed in a worker or lazily per card; the sides' documents only for the rendered view and the context folds.

Put the proposals, with the measurements, in a short document (`docs/review-performance.md`) and open a review of it with Hakan (`atm review create --task <this> --file docs/review-performance.md`) before building; then the chosen ones.

## Tests
The performance budget for a long review (first file drawn, a scroll to the end) in `performance.spec.ts`; unit tests for any paging or caching added.

tasks.name: Code review: a provisional task key's ~ gets into reviews: decisions don't reach the task, agents reuse ~KEY and fail
tasks.description:
Two reports from Hakan (2026-11-18), one cause.

1. **An approved review leaves its task waiting.** In CompMD, CR-2 and CR-3 are approved, but their task CMD-36 is still in review with `review_state: waiting`: the decision never reached it.
2. **Agents reuse a key with its `~` and fail.** `atm review` commands print a task's key as `~CMD-36`, agents pass that to the next command (`atm task state ~CMD-36 done`, `--task ~CMD-36`), and atm refuses it.

## Cause
A provisional key reads to people with a `~` before it (ADR-007 §3: `task_label` in [`project.rs`](crates/atm-lib/src/project.rs#L169-L187), `label_of` in [`keys.rs`](crates/atm-common/src/keys.rs#L65-L76)). The reviews use that **label** as the task's name where they need its **reference**: [`reviews.rs`](crates/atm-lib/src/reviews.rs) names the review's tasks with `project.task_label(t)` (lines 295, 418 and 467), so `review.md` stores `tasks: [~CMD-36]`; a decision, applied to each named task, finds no task `~CMD-36` and skips it without saying so. [`review_listen.rs`](crates/atm-lib/src/review_listen.rs#L182) prints the same label in `atm review watch`'s JSON.

## Change
- What a review stores and what atm prints for programs (`--json`, the watch's lines, the review's `tasks`) is the task's **key without `~`** (the key stays the reference while it is provisional; it follows the task when it becomes final, as `code_reviews` follows the review's UUID); the `~` only where people read it (plain output, the dashboard, which marks it itself).
- **Every command takes a key with a leading `~`** as the key itself (`resolve_task`), as `maintenance.rs` already strips it for one: what atm printed always works as input.
- **A decision that can't reach a named task says so** (an error or a warning in the command's output, naming the task), never a silent skip.
- **Reviews already written** with `~KEY` (CompMD's CR-1 to CR-3) read as `KEY`; and their decisions, approved before the fix, reach their tasks: `atm doctor` names a review whose decision its task doesn't have, and offers to apply it (or the next command that reads it does), so CMD-36 comes out of review as approved without anyone deciding again.
- The skills and `docs/agent/` say nothing of `~`; check that no example shows a key with it.

## Tests
atm-lib tests: a review of a provisional task stores and prints its key without `~`; its approval reaches the task; a `~KEY` resolves; a decision on a review naming a missing task is reported. CLI suite (`tests/scripts/reviews.test.mjs`): create a review of a provisional task, approve it, the task is approved; `atm task state ~KEY …` works; `review watch` prints the plain key. A test that a review stored with `~KEY` has its decision applied.

- Each folder row has a chevron (Lucide's, as the file cards' folds): a click, or ← and → on the focused row, collapses or expands it; its files and subfolders hide with it. A collapsed folder shows how many files it holds and, when any, how many of them have comments or aren't viewed yet.
- **Collapse all** and **Expand all** at the top of the tree (icon buttons, with titles).
- What is folded is kept per review while the page is open (and across a reload, in the session's storage), not written anywhere else.
- Going to a file (a click in the diffs, the next or previous change or comment, the address's `&file=`) opens the folders on its way, so the file it shows is always in view in the tree.
- The tree stays a tree for keyboards and screen readers (`role="tree"`, `aria-expanded` on folders).

Component tests (a folder collapses and expands, by click and keys; Collapse all and Expand all; a jump to a file in a collapsed folder opens it); an e2e test in `reviews.spec.ts`.
